> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://rain.one/docs/llms.txt

# Managing Liquidity

> Add and remove liquidity, read LP share balances

Liquidity in Rain markets is provided **per option**: you deposit base tokens into a
single option's AMM and receive LP shares for that option, which you later burn to
withdraw. This page covers adding liquidity, reading your LP share balance, and
removing liquidity. Builders return unsigned transactions you execute yourself — see
[Architecture](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Architecture.md).

Amounts are in base-token wei, `option` is 1-based, `slippageTolerance` is a
whole-percent bigint, and `deadline` is an absolute unix timestamp — see
[Conventions](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Conventions.md).

## Add liquidity

```typescript title="signature.ts" theme={null}
buildAddLiquidityTx(params: AddLiquidityTxParams & {
  walletAddress: `0x${string}`;
}): Promise<RawTransaction[]>
```

`buildAddLiquidityTx` deposits base tokens into one option's AMM. On-chain it encodes
the market contract's `enterLiquidity` function (there is no `addLiquidity` function),
and the corresponding real-time event is `liquidity` (`onLiquidity`), whose payload
field is `enterLiquidity`. It is async because it does real work before returning:

1. It reads the market's base token and checks the current allowance for
   `walletAddress` — if the allowance is too low, it prepends an exact-amount
   ERC-20 approval transaction.
2. It calculates slippage protection from the on-chain AMM reserves
   (`ammYesReserve` / `ammNoReserve`, proportionally) — but **only when you pass
   neither** `minYesToDeposit` nor `minNoToDeposit`.

```typescript title="add-liquidity.ts" theme={null}
import { Rain } from 'rain-sdk-v2';
import { parseUnits } from 'viem';

const rain = new Rain({ environment: 'development' });

// `wallet` below is your own executor — a viem WalletClient, an ethers Signer,
// or RainAA. `Rain` never signs. See Quickstart, "Execute the transactions".

const txs = await rain.buildAddLiquidityTx({
  marketContractAddress: '0xMarket',
  option: 1n,                              // 1-based option index
  totalAmountInWei: parseUnits('10', 6),   // 10 USDT (6 decimals)
  walletAddress: '0xYourWallet',
  slippageTolerance: 5n,                   // optional, default 5%
  deadline: BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 600), // optional — ABSOLUTE unix timestamp; default: now + 600 s
});

// txs = [approveTx?, addLiquidityTx] — sign and send IN ORDER
for (const tx of txs) {
  await wallet.sendTransaction(tx);
}
```

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| `marketContractAddress` | `` `0x${string}` `` | Yes | Market contract address |
| `option` | `bigint` | Yes | 1-based option index |
| `totalAmountInWei` | `bigint` | Yes | Deposit amount in base-token wei |
| `walletAddress` | `` `0x${string}` `` | Yes | User wallet, used for the allowance check |
| `minYesToDeposit` | `bigint` | No | Min Yes tokens to deposit. Auto-calculated from reserves **only when both min params are omitted**; if you pass only `minNoToDeposit`, this defaults to `0n` (no protection) |
| `minNoToDeposit` | `bigint` | No | Min No tokens to deposit. Auto-calculated from reserves **only when both min params are omitted**; if you pass only `minYesToDeposit`, this defaults to `0n` (no protection) |
| `slippageTolerance` | `bigint` | No | Whole-number percent (`5n` = 5%). Default 5% |
| `deadline` | `bigint` | No | Absolute unix timestamp in seconds. Default: now + 600 s |

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Pass both mins or neither.** Supplying only one disables auto-calculation for the
> other — it silently falls back to `0n`, leaving that leg with no slippage
> protection. If the AMM reserves are zero, both mins also silently become `0n`.

The returned array may or may not start with an approval transaction, depending on
your existing allowance — always iterate and send sequentially rather than assuming a
fixed length. Approvals are always for the **exact amount**; infinite approvals were
removed in v2.0.0.

## Read your LP share balance

```typescript title="signature.ts" theme={null}
getUserOptionLPShares(params: {
  marketContractAddress: `0x${string}`;
  option: bigint;
  userAddress: `0x${string}`;
}): Promise<bigint>
```

Returns the raw LP share balance a user holds for one option — this is the number you
pass to `buildRemoveLiquidityTx` as `lpShares`. Example:

```typescript title="get-lp-shares.ts" theme={null}
const lpShares = await rain.getUserOptionLPShares({
  marketContractAddress: '0xMarket',
  option: 1n,
  userAddress: '0xYourWallet',
});
// => 0n  (this user holds no LP shares in this market)
```

LP shares are a raw on-chain `bigint` — there is no formatted/decimal variant. To
withdraw a full position, pass the value back to `buildRemoveLiquidityTx` unchanged.

## Remove liquidity

```typescript title="signature.ts" theme={null}
buildRemoveLiquidityTx(params: RemoveLiquidityTxParams): Promise<RawTransaction>
```

`buildRemoveLiquidityTx` burns LP shares and withdraws the underlying tokens. No
approval is needed (you are burning shares, not spending tokens), so it returns a
**single** `RawTransaction` — but it is still `async`: before returning, it calls the
market's on-chain `getRemovedLiquidity` to compute the expected Yes/No amounts out and
applies your slippage tolerance to derive `minYesOut` / `minNoOut` — but only when you
pass **neither** of them explicitly.

```typescript title="remove-liquidity.ts" theme={null}
// 1. Read the LP position
const lpShares = await rain.getUserOptionLPShares({
  marketContractAddress: '0xMarket',
  option: 1n,
  userAddress: '0xYourWallet',
});

// 2. Build the withdrawal (full exit here)
const tx = await rain.buildRemoveLiquidityTx({
  marketContractAddress: '0xMarket',
  option: 1n,
  lpShares,
  slippageTolerance: 5n, // optional, default 5%
  deadline: BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 600), // optional — ABSOLUTE unix timestamp; default: now + 600 s
});

await wallet.sendTransaction(tx);
```

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| `marketContractAddress` | `` `0x${string}` `` | Yes | Market contract address |
| `option` | `bigint` | Yes | 1-based option index |
| `lpShares` | `bigint` | Yes | LP shares to burn (raw amount) |
| `minYesOut` | `bigint` | No | Min Yes tokens to receive. Auto-calculated via `getRemovedLiquidity` **only when both min params are omitted**; if you pass only `minNoOut`, this defaults to `0n` |
| `minNoOut` | `bigint` | No | Min No tokens to receive. Auto-calculated **only when both min params are omitted**; if you pass only `minYesOut`, this defaults to `0n` |
| `slippageTolerance` | `bigint` | No | Whole-number percent (`5n` = 5%). Default 5% |
| `deadline` | `bigint` | No | Absolute unix timestamp in seconds. Default: now + 600 s |

As with adding liquidity: pass **both** min params or **neither**. Supplying only
one leaves the other at `0n` — no slippage protection on that leg.

To react to liquidity changes in real time, subscribe to `RainSocket.onLiquidity` and
`RainSocket.onRemoveLiquidity` for the pool — see
[Real-time events](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/WebSockets-and-Live-Data.md).

## Related pages

* [AMM trading](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Trading-and-positions.md) — entering and selling options against the pool you provide liquidity to
* [Conventions](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Conventions.md) — option indexing, slippage, deadlines
* [Market fees](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Creating-a-Market.md#market-fees) — liquidity-related fees at market creation

# Split and Merge

> Split collateral into full share sets and merge them back

Every option in a Rain market has a Yes side and a No side. **Split** converts base tokens into an equal number of Yes and No shares of one option — a complete set — and **merge** does the reverse, burning matched Yes+No pairs and returning base tokens. Splitting 5 USDT yields 5 Yes shares *and* 5 No shares.

This gives you a second way in and out of a market besides trading:

* **Entering both sides at once** — `buildSplitTx` is an alternative to `buildEnterOptionTx` for entering a market. You receive both sides without moving the AMM price or crossing the book, and can then sell or place orders for the side you don't want via [AMM trading](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Trading-and-positions.md) or the [Order book](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Order-Book.md).
* **Exiting a matched pair** — if you hold equal Yes and No shares of an option, merging converts them straight back to base tokens instead of selling each side separately.

Neither operation charges a fee, and neither moves the market: on-chain, `split` pulls
exactly `amount` base tokens and credits exactly `amount` shares on each side, and
`merge` burns the pairs and returns exactly `amount` base tokens — a precise 1:1
conversion both ways that never touches the AMM reserves or the order book (verified
against the deployed `SplitMergeFacet` contract). Two constraints to know:

* Shares locked in escrow by resting sell orders don't count toward a merge — cancel
  the orders first (see [Claiming](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Claiming.md#getusersharesinescrow) for the
  escrow read).
* Both operations revert once the option is finalized (the claim phase) — splitting
  and merging are trading-phase tools.

## buildSplitTx

```typescript title="signature.ts" theme={null}
buildSplitTx(
  params: SplitTxParams & { walletAddress: `0x${string}` }
): Promise<RawTransaction[]>
```

**Async**: splitting spends base tokens, so the builder checks `walletAddress`'s allowance and prepends an approval transaction when needed.

```typescript title="split.ts" theme={null}
const txs = await rain.buildSplitTx({
  marketContractAddress: '0xMarket',
  option: 1n,                 // 1-based option index
  amount: 5_000_000n,         // 5 USDT (6 decimals) -> 5 Yes + 5 No shares
  walletAddress: '0xYourWallet',
});

// txs = [approveTx?, splitTx] — send in order
```

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| `marketContractAddress` | `` `0x${string}` `` | Yes | Market contract address. |
| `option` | `bigint` | Yes | Option index, 1-based. |
| `amount` | `bigint` | Yes | Base tokens to split, in token wei. |
| `walletAddress` | `` `0x${string}` `` | Yes | Your address, used for the allowance check. |

## buildMergeTx

```typescript title="signature.ts" theme={null}
buildMergeTx(params: MergeTxParams): RawTransaction
```

`buildMergeTx` is **synchronous** — it returns a single `RawTransaction`, no `await`. No approval is needed: the contract burns your Yes+No share pairs and returns base tokens.

```typescript title="merge.ts" theme={null}
// Check how many shares you hold on each side first
const yesShares = await rain.getUserOptionShares({
  marketContractAddress: '0xMarket',
  option: 1n,
  optionSide: 1,               // Yes
  userAddress: '0xYourWallet',
});
const noShares = await rain.getUserOptionShares({
  marketContractAddress: '0xMarket',
  option: 1n,
  optionSide: 2,               // No
  userAddress: '0xYourWallet',
});

const mergeable = yesShares < noShares ? yesShares : noShares;

const tx = rain.buildMergeTx({   // no await — synchronous
  marketContractAddress: '0xMarket',
  option: 1n,
  amount: mergeable,             // raw shares amount
});
```

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| `marketContractAddress` | `` `0x${string}` `` | Yes | Market contract address. |
| `option` | `bigint` | Yes | Option index, 1-based. |
| `amount` | `bigint` | Yes | Number of Yes+No pairs to merge, in raw share units (query balances with `getUserOptionShares`). |

## Related

* [AMM trading](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Trading-and-positions.md) — sell the unwanted side of a split, or buy the missing side before a merge.
* [Order book](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Order-Book.md) — place limit orders for either side on order-book markets.
* [Real-time events](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/WebSockets-and-Live-Data.md) — `split/{poolId}` and `merge/{poolId}` socket channels fire on every split and merge.

# Protocol Fees and Builder Rewards

> The 5% trading fee, who receives each slice, the RAIN buyback-and-burn, and referrer rewards

Every fill on a Rain market — AMM trade or order-book match — charges the taker a
**5% fee on the traded amount**. The fee is taken on top of the trade and never
enters the option's prize pot, so winners always claim the full pot with no
settlement deduction. All numbers on this page are verified against the deployed
contracts and are identical on development, stage, and production.

## How the fee splits

| Slice | Rate | Who receives it |
| - | - | - |
| Liquidity reward | 1.2% | Whoever provided the liquidity being consumed — **AMM LPs** on AMM trades, the **maker** (resting order's owner) on order-book fills. See the breakdown below. |
| RAIN buyback-and-burn | 2.5% | Nobody — the platform share is swapped to RAIN on-chain at claim time and **burned** |
| Market creator | 1.0% | The pool owner, at claim time (split with a referrer if one is set — see below) |
| Resolver — oracle part | 0.1% | The resolution oracle |
| Resolver — closer part | 0.2% | Whoever triggers the market closure |

These are governed by per-market fee parameters readable on-chain from any market
contract (`liquidityFee()`, `platformFee()`, `creatorFee()`, `resultResolverFee()`,
`closingFee()`). They are set at the factory and tunable by Rain without a code
change, so treat the percentages above as the current configuration rather than
immutable constants.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The raw on-chain values are expressed **out of 1,000**, not in basis points:
> `liquidityFee() = 12` means 1.2%, `platformFee() = 25` means 2.5%, and so on. Keep
> this in mind when reading the values yourself — and see the naming warning below
> about the SDK's `getCreateMarketFees`.

## AMM trades vs order-book fills

The total is **5% on both trading models** — only the liquidity slice changes
hands differently:

| | AMM trade | Order-book fill |
| - | - | - |
| Protocol slices (burn + creator + resolver) | 3.8% | 3.8% |
| Liquidity slice (1.2%) | Swap fee accrued to the option's **LP reward accumulator**; LPs collect it automatically when they add or remove liquidity | **Maker rebate** (`MAKER_REBATE_FEE = 12`) paid directly to the resting order's owner on each fill |
| **Taker pays** | **5.0%** | **5.0%** |

There is no separate LP swap fee on order-book fills — the maker rebate takes the
liquidity slice's place, compensating the maker for resting on the book. A
separate order-execution fee parameter also exists but is currently set to zero.

## Referrer rewards

Markets can carry a `referrer` address, set at creation by the Rain platform. When
one is set, the referrer receives **half of the creator fee** (0.5% of volume) at
claim time and the pool owner keeps the other half; with no referrer the creator
keeps the full 1.0%. This is the on-chain half of Rain's builder-reward program —
the program's terms themselves (who qualifies, how the referrer gets attached) are
managed by Rain, not by the SDK.

## The oracle fixed fee is currently off

The factory also defines a fixed per-option oracle fee for market creation
(`oracleFixedFee()`), historically intended as a \$1-per-option charge for
AI-resolved markets. It is **currently set to zero on all three environments** —
appeals fund the oracle out of the resolver share instead. This matches what
[`getCreateMarketFees`](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Creating-a-Market#getcreatemarketfees) reads live
(`oracleFeePerOption: 0n`).

## What has no fee

* **Split and merge** — exact 1:1 both ways; see [Split & merge](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Split-and-Merge.md).
* **Claiming winnings** — winners receive their full payout; the 5% was already
  collected from takers during trading.
* **Cancelling orders** — escrowed tokens or shares are returned in full.

## A naming trap in the SDK

`getCreateMarketFees` returns a field called `liquidityFeeBps`. Despite the name,
it is the **raw on-chain `liquidityFee` value** (`12n`), which the contract applies
out of 1,000 — the real per-trade LP fee is **1.2%**, not 12 basis points. The
SDK's own create-market approval math divides the value by 10,000, so it
contributes only a small (\~0.12%) buffer to the [create-market approval
amount](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Creating-a-Market.md#market-fees). Don't surface `liquidityFeeBps`
as "the trading fee" in a UI without converting it.

![Main Protocol Fees](https://mintcdn.com/rain-2dc0bd37/Dc44C5tw3FsFxiRq/images/Main-Protocol-Fees.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=Dc44C5tw3FsFxiRq\&q=85\&s=4bce66943ef4ceb56f04e6365794f01e)

## Builder Rewards

Our Builder Program is designed for those launching their own frontends or niche
applications using the Rain SDK. As a builder, you earn a direct share of the
activity your platform generates.

* **Baseline reward** — builders receive a percentage of the total trading volume
  generated by their application. The exact percentage will be finalized through a
  DAO decision. On-chain this is delivered through the `referrer` mechanism
  described above.
* **Stacking rewards** — builders can significantly increase these earnings by
  taking on multiple roles. If you act as the market creator, the initial liquidity
  provider, and the resolver, your total rewards can reach up to **2.5%** of the
  volume (1.0% creator + 1.2% liquidity + 0.3% resolver).
* **Liquidity providers** earn **1.2%** of the trading volume their specific pool
  generates, collected automatically when they add or remove liquidity.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Building on the Entropy Layer instead? Its markets draw from a single shared
> liquidity pool and use a different fee model — see
> [Fees on the Entropy Layer](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Entropy-Layer/Fee-Structure.md).

## Related pages

* [Creating a market](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Creating-a-Market.md#market-fees) — creation-time fees and approval amounts
* [Disputes and appeals](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Disputes-Appeals.md) — dispute and appeal fees (separate from the trading fee)
* [Closing a market](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Closing-a-Market.md) — resolver bonds
* [Managing liquidity](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Rain-SDK/Liquidity.md) — how LPs collect their accrued 1.2%
* [Fees on the Entropy Layer](https://rain.one/docs/For-Developers/Entropy-Layer/Fee-Structure.md) — the shared-pool fee model for RNG markets

# Rain SDK V2

TypeScript SDK for the Rain prediction markets protocol on Arbitrum One. Provides transaction builders for market creation, trading, liquidity management, order book operations, dispute resolution, and smart account (Account Abstraction) support.

## ⚠️ Security notice — upgrade to >= 2.5.0

Versions **below 2.5.0** build **sell** transactions with no slippage protection by
default: `buildSellOptionTx` defaulted `minAmountOut` to `0` and the documented
`slippageTolerance` option was ignored, exposing sells to MEV/sandwich loss.
**Fixed in 2.5.0** — sells now quote `getSellProceeds` on-chain and apply
`slippageTolerance` (default 5%). Versions `<2.5.0` are deprecated on npm.

Migration is one line: **`buildSellOptionTx` is now async** — add `await`.

```typescript
// before (< 2.5.0)
const tx = rain.buildSellOptionTx({ /* ... */ });
// after (>= 2.5.0)
const tx = await rain.buildSellOptionTx({ /* ... */ });
```

## Installation

```bash
npm install rain-sdk-v2 viem
```

### Optional (for Smart Account / Account Abstraction)

```bash
npm install @alchemy/aa-core @account-kit/infra @account-kit/wallet-client
```

## Quick Start

```typescript
import { Rain, RainAA, TradingModel, OptionSide } from 'rain-sdk-v2';
import { createWalletClient, custom, parseUnits, parseEther } from 'viem';
import { arbitrum } from 'viem/chains';

// Initialize SDK
const rain = new Rain({
  environment: 'development', // 'development' | 'stage' | 'production'
  rpcUrl: 'https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc', // optional; falls back to a public RPC (pass your own in production)
});

// Get environment config
const config = rain.getEnvironmentConfig();
console.log(config.market_factory_address); // Factory contract
console.log(config.tokens.usdt.address);    // USDT token address
console.log(config.tokens.rain.address);    // RAIN token address
console.log(config.tokens.usdr.address);    // USDR token address
console.log(config.tokens.usdt.decimals);   // 6
console.log(config.tokens.rain.decimals);   // 18
console.log(config.tokens.usdr.decimals);   // 18

// Get token config by address
const tokenInfo = rain.getTokenConfig('0x...');
console.log(tokenInfo?.decimals, tokenInfo?.symbol);

// USDR token ABI (ERC20 + AccessControl + EIP-2612 permit, role-gated mint/burn)
import { USDRAbi } from 'rain-sdk-v2';
```

---

## Classes

### `Rain`

Stateless class for building transactions and querying on-chain data. Does not require a wallet.

#### Constructor

```typescript
const rain = new Rain(config?: RainCoreConfig);
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `environment` | `'development' \| 'stage' \| 'production'` | `'development'` | Target environment |
| `rpcUrl` | `string` | Fixed public RPC | Custom Arbitrum RPC URL. Omitting it uses a single deterministic public RPC; in `production` this also emits a `console.warn` — pass a dedicated endpoint. |
| `apiUrl` | `string` | From environment | Custom API URL |

---

### `RainAA`

Stateful class for smart account (Account Abstraction) management with Alchemy gas sponsorship.

> ⚠️ **Browser-only.** `RainAA` persists session keys in `indexedDB`, so it is **not supported in Node.js or SSR** — session methods throw a descriptive error in those environments. For server-side flows use the stateless `Rain` class (transaction building and on-chain reads), which runs anywhere.

#### Constructor

```typescript
const rainAA = new RainAA(config: RainConfig);
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `walletClient` | `WalletClient` | Yes | Viem wallet client |
| `alchemyApiKey` | `string` | Yes | Alchemy API key |
| `paymasterPolicyId` | `string` | Yes | Alchemy paymaster policy ID |
| `chain` | `Chain` | Yes | Viem chain (e.g. `arbitrum`) |
| `rpcUrl` | `string` | No | Custom RPC URL |

#### Methods

##### `connect()`

Initializes the smart account. Returns the smart account address.

```typescript
const smartAccountAddress = await rainAA.connect();
```

##### `sendTransaction(rawTx: RawTransaction)`

Sends a transaction from the smart account (gas-sponsored).

```typescript
const hash = await rainAA.sendTransaction(rawTx);
```

##### `disconnect()`

Resets the connection state.

```typescript
rainAA.disconnect();
```

##### `address` (getter)

Returns the smart account address. Throws if not connected.

##### `client` (getter)

Returns the smart wallet client instance. Throws if not connected.

---

## Transaction Builders

All transaction builders return `RawTransaction` (or `RawTransaction[]` for multi-step operations):

```typescript
interface RawTransaction {
  to: `0x${string}`;
  data: `0x${string}`;
  value?: bigint;
}
```

---

### Market Creation

#### `buildCreateMarketTx(params: CreateMarketTxParams): Promise<RawTransaction[]>`

Creates a new prediction market. Returns approval TX (if needed) + createPool TX.

```typescript
const config = rain.getEnvironmentConfig();

// Create market with USDT (6 decimals)
const txs = await rain.buildCreateMarketTx({
  marketQuestion: 'Will ETH reach $5000 by end of 2025?',
  marketOptions: ['Yes', 'No'],
  marketTags: ['crypto'],
  marketDescription: 'Prediction on ETH price target',
  isPublic: true,
  isPublicPoolResolverAi: true, // true = AI resolver, false = manual resolver
  creator: '0x...', // smart account or EOA address
  startTime: BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 120), // 2 min from now
  endTime: BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 86400), // 24h from now
  no_of_options: 2n,
  disputeTimer: 259200, // oracle end time duration in seconds (e.g. 259200 = 3 days)
  inputAmountWei: parseUnits('10', 6), // 10 USDT
  barValues: [50, 50], // probability distribution (0-100, sums to 100)
  initialYesPrices: [500000000000000000n, 500000000000000000n], // optional, 1e18 scale (50% = 5e17)
  baseToken: config.tokens.usdt.address, // USDT
  tradingModel: TradingModel.AMM, // AMM = 0, OrderBook = 1
  marketImage: 'https://cdn.example.com/market-image.png',
});

// Create market with RAIN token (18 decimals)
const txsRain = await rain.buildCreateMarketTx({
  ...params,
  inputAmountWei: parseUnits('10', 18), // 10 RAIN
  baseToken: config.tokens.rain.address, // RAIN token
});

// Approval for USDT: liquidity + (oracleFixedFeePerOption * numberOfOptions)
// Approval for RAIN: liquidity + (numberOfOptions * 20% of liquidity)
// e.g. 1000 RAIN with 5 options → 1000 + (5 * 200) = 2000 RAIN approval
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `marketQuestion` | `string` | The market question |
| `marketOptions` | `string[]` | Option labels. 1 = binary (single Yes/No) market; 2+ = multi-outcome. Length must equal `no_of_options` |
| `marketTags` | `string[]` | Tags (1-3) |
| `marketDescription` | `string` | Description |
| `isPublic` | `boolean` | Public market |
| `isPublicPoolResolverAi` | `boolean` | `true` for AI resolver, `false` for manual |
| `creator` | `0x${string}` | Creator/pool owner address |
| `startTime` | `bigint` | Unix timestamp (seconds) |
| `endTime` | `bigint` | Unix timestamp (seconds) |
| `no_of_options` | `bigint` | Number of options |
| `inputAmountWei` | `bigint` | Initial liquidity in base token wei |
| `disputeTimer` | `number` | Oracle end time duration in seconds (e.g. 259200 = 3 days). Auto-set from environment config |
| `barValues` | `number[]` | Probability distribution (0-100 scale) |
| `initialYesPrices` | `bigint[]` | *(Optional)* Initial Yes prices per option in 1e18 scale (e.g. `500000000000000000n` = 50%). Defaults to 50% for both AMM and OrderBook |
| `baseToken` | `0x${string}` | Base token address (USDT or RAIN) |
| `tradingModel` | `TradingModel` | `AMM (0)` or `OrderBook (1)` |
| `marketImage` | `string` | Market image URL (required) |

> **Constraints (validated, throws if violated):** `no_of_options ≥ 2`; `marketOptions`, `barValues`, and (if provided) `initialYesPrices` must each have length `no_of_options`; every `barValue` must be within `0–100` and the set must **sum to 100**; each `initialYesPrice` must be within `(0, 1e18)` exclusive. Previously out-of-spec bar values were silently redistributed onto the last option — they are now rejected.

### Trading

#### `buildEnterOptionTx(params): Promise<RawTransaction[]>`

Buy shares of an option (AMM trade). Automatically reads the market's base token, checks allowance, includes approval TX if needed, and calculates slippage protection via on-chain `getEntryShares`.

```typescript
const txs = await rain.buildEnterOptionTx({
  marketContractAddress: '0x...',
  selectedOption: 1n, // 1-based option index
  optionSide: OptionSide.Yes, // Yes = 1, No = 2
  buyAmountInWei: parseUnits('5', 6), // 5 USDT (or parseUnits('5', 18) for RAIN)
  walletAddress: '0x...', // user's wallet address
  slippageTolerance: 5n, // optional, default 5% — percentage tolerance for minSharesOut
  deadline: BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 600), // optional — absolute unix timestamp; omit for a default 10-min window
});
// Returns [approveTx?, enterOptionTx]
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `marketContractAddress` | `0x${string}` | Market contract address |
| `selectedOption` | `bigint` | Option index (1-based) |
| `optionSide` | `OptionSide` | `Yes (1)` or `No (2)` |
| `buyAmountInWei` | `bigint` | Amount in base token wei |
| `walletAddress` | `0x${string}` | User's wallet address (for allowance check) |
| `minSharesOut` | `bigint` | *(Optional)* Minimum shares to receive. Auto-calculated from `getEntryShares` with slippage if not set |
| `slippageTolerance` | `bigint` | *(Optional)* Slippage percentage (e.g. `5n` = 5%). Default: 5% |
| `deadline` | `bigint` | *(Optional)* Absolute unix timestamp in seconds, e.g. `BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now()/1000) + 600)`. Omit for a default 10-min window. A small duration like `600n` is **rejected** (`RainValidationError`). |

> **Note:** Approval is handled automatically. The SDK reads `baseToken` from the market contract and checks allowance before building transactions. Slippage protection is auto-calculated: the SDK calls `getEntryShares` on-chain to get expected shares, then applies the slippage tolerance.

---

#### `buildSellOptionTx(params): Promise<RawTransaction>`

Market-sell shares of an option into the resting buy order book. No approval needed (you're selling shares, not tokens). Slippage protection is auto-calculated from on-chain `getSellProceeds` (default 5%) when `minAmountOut` is omitted. Pass `minAmountOut: 0n` to opt out explicitly.

```typescript
const tx = await rain.buildSellOptionTx({
  marketContractAddress: '0x...',
  selectedOption: 1n, // 1-based option index
  optionSide: OptionSide.Yes, // Yes = 1, No = 2
  sharesAmount: parseUnits('10', 6), // shares to sell
  slippageTolerance: 5n, // optional, default 5%
  deadline: BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 600), // optional — absolute unix timestamp; omit for a default 10-min window
});
// Returns a single RawTransaction (no approval needed)
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `marketContractAddress` | `0x${string}` | Market contract address |
| `selectedOption` | `bigint` | Option index (1-based) |
| `optionSide` | `OptionSide` | `Yes (1)` or `No (2)` |
| `sharesAmount` | `bigint` | Number of shares to sell |
| `minAmountOut` | `bigint` | *(Optional)* Minimum base tokens to receive. Auto-calculated from `getSellProceeds` with slippage if not set. Pass `0n` to opt out |
| `slippageTolerance` | `bigint` | *(Optional)* Slippage percentage (e.g. `5n` = 5%). Default: 5% |
| `deadline` | `bigint` | *(Optional)* Absolute unix timestamp in seconds, e.g. `BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now()/1000) + 600)`. Omit for a default 10-min window. A small duration like `600n` is **rejected** (`RainValidationError`). |

### Order Book

#### `buildPlaceBuyOrderTx(params): Promise<RawTransaction[]>`

Place a limit buy order. Automatically checks allowance and includes approval TX if needed.

```typescript
const txs = await rain.buildPlaceBuyOrderTx({
  marketContractAddress: '0x...',
  option: 1n,
  optionSide: OptionSide.Yes,
  price: parseEther('0.5'), // 50% price in 1e18 scale
  amount: parseUnits('10', 6), // 10 USDT
  postOnly: false, // optional, defaults to false. Set true for maker-only (reverts OrderWouldCross if it would cross the book)
  walletAddress: '0x...', // user's wallet address
});
// Returns [approveTx?, placeBuyOrderTx]
```

> **Note:** Approval is handled automatically. Available when AMM pool is closed.
>
> **`postOnly`:** When `true`, the matching loop is skipped — the order rests directly. If `price` would cross a resting ask the call reverts `OrderWouldCross`, so the caller is never charged taker fees. When `false` (default), behaviour is unchanged: matches the sell book first and rests only the residual.

#### `buildPlaceSellOrderTx(params: PlaceSellOrderTxParams): RawTransaction`

Place a limit sell order.

```typescript
const tx = rain.buildPlaceSellOrderTx({
  marketContractAddress: '0x...',
  option: 1n,
  optionSide: OptionSide.Yes,
  price: parseEther('0.7'), // 70% price in 1e18 scale
  shares: 5000000n, // shares to sell (from getUserOptionShares)
  postOnly: false, // optional, defaults to false. Set true for maker-only (reverts OrderWouldCross if it would cross the book)
});
```

> **Note:** No approval needed. Shares are escrowed by the contract.
>
> **`postOnly`:** Same semantics as `buildPlaceBuyOrderTx` — `true` rejects orders that would immediately cross the buy book (revert `OrderWouldCross`); `false` matches the buy book first and rests only the residual.

#### `buildCancelBuyOrdersTx(params: CancelBuyOrdersTxParams): RawTransaction`

Cancel one or more buy orders.

```typescript
const tx = rain.buildCancelBuyOrdersTx({
  marketContractAddress: '0x...',
  option: 1n,
  optionSides: [1, 1], // Yes, Yes
  prices: [parseEther('0.5'), parseEther('0.6')],
  orderIDs: [1n, 2n], // from PlaceBuyOrder event
});
```

#### `buildCancelSellOrdersTx(params: CancelSellOrdersTxParams): RawTransaction`

Cancel one or more sell orders. Same interface as `buildCancelBuyOrdersTx`.

#### `buildCalculateWinnerTx(params: CalculateWinnerTxParams): Promise<RawTransaction>`

Calculate winner via the oracle resolver. Must be called before `claim`. Reads `optionResolver(option)` from the market and calls `calculateWinner()` on that resolver contract.

  marketContractAddress: '0x...',
  option: 1n,
});

---

#### `buildExtendTimeTx(params: ExtendTimeTxParams): Promise<RawTransaction>`

Extend the resolution time of a market option. Requires a signature from the oracle backend (obtained via `signOraclesExtendTime` API). Reads `optionResolver(option)` from the market and calls `extendTime(newEndTime, signature)` on that resolver contract.

```typescript
// 1. Get the signature from the API
const signResult = await rain.signOraclesExtendTime(
  { contractAddress: '0x...', walletAddress: '0x...' },
  accessToken
);

// 2. Build the extend time transaction
const tx = await rain.buildExtendTimeTx({
  marketContractAddress: '0x...',
  option: 1n,
  newEndTime: BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 86400), // extend by 1 day
  signature: signResult.signature, // from API
});
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `marketContractAddress` | `0x${string}` | Market contract address |
| `option` | `bigint` | Option index (1-based) |
| `newEndTime` | `bigint` | New end time as unix timestamp (seconds) |
| `signature` | `0x${string}` | Backend signature from `signOraclesExtendTime` |

## Authentication

### `login(params: LoginParams): Promise<LoginResult>`

Wallet-based login to the Rain backend.

#### `signLoginMessage(walletClient, walletAddress)`

Signs the lowercased wallet address using `personal_sign`. This signature is required for login.

```typescript
import { signLoginMessage } from 'rain-sdk-v2';

const walletClient = createWalletClient({ chain: arbitrum, transport: custom(window.ethereum) });
const signature = await signLoginMessage(walletClient, '0x...' as `0x${string}`);
```

#### `login(params)`

```typescript
const result = await rain.login({
  signature, // from signLoginMessage
  walletAddress: '0x...', // EOA address
  smartWalletAddress: '0x...', // optional — defaults to walletAddress for plain-EOA integrations
  referredBy: 'CODE', // optional referral code
});

console.log(result.accessToken); // JWT token
console.log(result.userId); // Backend user ID
```

```typescript
const config = rain.getEnvironmentConfig();

config.tokens.rain.symbol    // "RAIN"
```

## Typical Flow

```
1. Create Market (buildCreateMarketTx)
2. Wait for startTime to pass
3. Enter Option (buildEnterOptionTx) / Split (buildSplitTx)
4. Place Orders (buildPlaceBuyOrderTx / buildPlaceSellOrderTx)
5. Wait for endTime to pass
6. Close Pool (buildClosePoolAITx / buildClosePoolManualTx)
7. Calculate Winner (buildCalculateWinnerTx)
8. Check if claimed (getOptionClaimed) — optional
9. Claim (buildClaimTx)
```

If disputed:
```
6b. Open Dispute (buildOpenDisputeTx)
6c. Appeal (buildOpenDisputeTx again)
```

If extending time:
```
5b. Extend Time (signOraclesExtendTime API → buildExtendTimeTx)
```

### Leaderboard

Public endpoints — no access token required. Boards are served from a materialized document rebuilt by a cron (~20 min), so changes appear after the next tick rather than on the next request.

```typescript
// Get a ranked leaderboard — one board per (board, window, category)
const board = await rain.getLeaderboard({
  board: 'profit',        // 'profit' (net realized PnL) or 'correct_calls' (sum of 1 − entryPrice over winning positions)
  window: 'all_time',     // 'all_time' (default) or 'monthly' (current UTC calendar month)
  category: 'Crypto',     // optional, case-insensitive; omit for the global board
  limit: 10,              // up to the stored cap of 100 (default 10)
});
// board.data = { board, window, category, categoryLabel, period, limit, totalRanked, priceBasis, entries, lastUpdatedAt }
// Each entry carries all four table columns — profit, correctCalls, winRate, trades —
// whichever board is sorting, so switching the sorted column needs no second request.

// Search traders on a board — the leaderboard's trader search box
const found = await rain.searchLeaderboard({
  q: '0x742d',            // wallet address, address fragment (with/without 0x, prefix/middle/tail), or user id
  board: 'profit',        // required — searches the stored board for this (board, window, category)
  window: 'all_time',     // optional, default 'all_time'
  category: 'Crypto',     // optional; omit for the global board
  limit: 10,              // up to 50 (default 10)
});
// found.data = { board, window, category, period, query, matched, searchedTop, totalRanked, lastUpdatedAt, results }
// `results` are the same entry objects getLeaderboard returns, in rank order.
// Scoped to the stored board — a trader outside the top N is simply not found.
// Empty `results` means "not on this board"; `searchedTop` + `totalRanked` let you
// say "not in the top 100" precisely. Queries under 2 characters return empty, not a 400.

// Get a trader's most recent trades — the rows inside an expanded leaderboard row
const recent = await rain.getTraderRecentTrades({
  userId: '...',          // from a leaderboard entry's `userId`
  limit: 5,               // rendered rows (a multi-side trade flattens into more lines), up to 25 (default 5)
});
// recent.data = { userId, limit, trades }
// Each trade: { action ('Buy'|'Sell'), origin, transactionHash, tradedAt, poolId, question,
//               poolImage, subPoolId, subQuestion, side (1=YES, 2=NO), optionName, shares,
//               amountUSD, pricePerShare, priceCents, status ('open'|'pending'|'settled'),
//               pnlScope, pnlUSD }
// Directional trades only (origin ∈ {enter, orderFill}), newest first — and unlike the
// track-record endpoint, OPEN positions are included (status 'open').
// `pnlUSD` is POSITION-level, not per-fill: several trades in the same market report the
// same number. Null until settled; `amountUSD`/`pnlUSD` are dollars × 1e6.

// Get categories that currently have a ranked board (feeds the category filter)
const categories = await rain.getLeaderboardCategories();
// categories.data = [{ category: 'CRYPTO', label: 'Crypto' }, ...]
// Pass `category` back as the `category` param of getLeaderboard.
```

**Notes:**
- **Units:** every `*USD` number (including `profit` and `score` on the profit board) is **dollars × 1e6** — divide by 1,000,000 to display. E.g. `profit: 887505347` is **$887.51**.
- **Monthly window** buckets on when PnL *settled*, not when the position was opened; `window: 'monthly'` always means the current UTC month (`period` reports it as `YYYY-MM`).
- **Only positive scores are ranked.** An unknown `category` returns an empty board, not a 400.
- **Top-N only** — there is no rank-of-user lookup. Empty `entries` with `lastUpdatedAt: null` means the cron hasn't built the board yet; empty with a timestamp means nobody qualifies.
- The client can highlight the viewer's own row by matching `userId` in `entries`.

## Helpers & Execution

### Executing transactions

Builders return unsigned `RawTransaction[]` where index 0 may be an ERC-20
approval. `rain.execute()` sends them in order and waits for each receipt before
the next — so the main transaction never front-runs its approval:

```typescript
const txs = await rain.buildEnterOptionTx({ /* ... */ });

await rain.execute(txs, {
  send: (tx) => walletClient.sendTransaction({ to: tx.to, data: tx.data, value: tx.value ?? 0n }),
  wait: (hash) => publicClient.waitForTransactionReceipt({ hash }),
});
```

The executor is pluggable — adapt `{ send, wait? }` to viem, ethers, RainAA, or
your own KMS. Also available as the standalone `executeTxs(txs, executor)`.

### Amount conversion

Convert between human-readable amounts and base units using the token's
configured decimals — no need to track that USDT is 6 and RAIN is 18:

```typescript
rain.parseAmount('5', usdtAddress);        // 5_000_000n
rain.formatAmount(5_000_000n, usdtAddress); // '5'
```

### Typed pool data

`getPublicPools` / `getPrivatePools` return `ApiResponse<PaginatedPools>`, and
socket event payloads type their `pool` / `subPool` fields as `Pool` / `SubPool`.
Import the DTOs to annotate your own code:

```typescript
import type { Pool, SubPool, PaginatedPools } from 'rain-sdk-v2';
```

### Socket event names

Use `RAIN_SOCKET_EVENTS` for correctly-spelled event identifiers with the
low-level `.on()` API (some raw wire names are misspelled upstream):

```typescript
import { RAIN_SOCKET_EVENTS } from 'rain-sdk-v2';
socket.on(RAIN_SOCKET_EVENTS.disputeTimeExtended, poolId, handler);
```

### Token expiry

`login()` returns `expiresAt` (unix seconds, decoded from the JWT) so you can
renew before it lapses:

```typescript
const { accessToken, expiresAt } = await rain.login({ /* ... */ });
```

## Error Handling & Validation

### Build-time validation

Transaction builders validate their inputs synchronously — before any encoding
or broadcast — and throw `RainValidationError` on the common footguns:

- `deadline` must be an **absolute unix timestamp** (seconds), not a duration.
  `deadline: 600n` is rejected; use `BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now()/1000) + 600)`.
- `slippageTolerance` is a **whole percent** (`5n` = 5%), and must be `0–100`.
- `option` / `selectedOption` are **1-based** (the first option is `1`, never `0`).

```typescript
import { RainValidationError } from 'rain-sdk-v2';

try {
  await rain.buildEnterOptionTx({ /* ... */, deadline: 600n });
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof RainValidationError) {
    console.error(err.field, err.message); // 'deadline', 'Invalid deadline: ...'
  }
}
```

### API errors

REST methods throw `RainApiError` (a subclass of `Error`) on non-2xx responses,
carrying structured fields so you can branch on `code` instead of parsing strings:

```typescript
import { RainApiError } from 'rain-sdk-v2';

try {
  await rain.getSomeData(/* ... */);
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof RainApiError) {
    console.error(err.status, err.code, err.endpoint, err.body);
    // code: 'NOT_FOUND' | 'UNAUTHORIZED' | 'FORBIDDEN' | 'RATE_LIMITED' | 'SERVER_ERROR' | 'UNKNOWN'
  }
}
```

Legitimate empty states are **not** errors: `getPnlByPoolId` (no position) and
`getTokenPrice` (non-whitelisted token) return `{ statusCode: 200, data: null }`
rather than throwing on a 404.

pragma solidity 0.8.26;

/**
 * @title IClaim
 * @author Rain Team
 * @notice Interface for the claim facet.
 * @dev Defines the external functions for claiming rewards within the Diamond architecture.
 */
interface IClaim {
    /* ===================================== FUNCTIONS ===================================== */

    /**
     * @notice Allows users to claim their winnings or liquidity rewards after an option has resolved.
     * @dev This function verifies whether the winner has been determined for the given option.
     *      - In public pools, it ensures the oracle has finalized the winner.
     *      - The function checks if the caller has already claimed their rewards for this option.
     *      - Rewards are calculated based on LP shares and winning-side shares.
     * @param option The option ID to claim rewards for.
     * @notice Reverts if:
     *      - The option is invalid.
     *      - The winner has not been determined.
     *      - The option is still open.
     *      - The user has already claimed rewards for this option.
     *      - The user is not eligible to claim any rewards.
     * @notice Emits a `Claim` event upon successful reward distribution.
     */
    function claim(uint256 option) external;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity 0.8.26;

/**
 * @title IInfo
 * @author Rain Team
 * @notice Interface for the rain pool info facet.
 * @dev Defines the external helper functions for the rain pool within the Diamond architecture.
 */
interface IInfo {
    /* ===================================== FUNCTIONS ===================================== */

    /**
     * @notice Returns the total number of active or created orders in the system.
     * @return The total number of orders.
     */
    function totalOrders() external returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the dynamic payout amount for a specific user on a specific option.
     * @param user The address of the user to calculate the dynamic payout for.
     * @param option The option to calculate the dynamic payout for.
     * @return dynamicPayout The amount of dynamic payout the user is eligible to receive for each side.
     */
    function getDynamicPayout(address user, uint256 option) external view returns (uint256[] memory dynamicPayout);

    /**
     * @notice Computes the amount of shares returned on the given amount for the specified option and side.
     * @param option The index of the option being evaluated.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @param amount The amount being added to the option.
     * @return returnedShares returned shares of the option side after adding the specified amount.
     * @return expectedReward returned expected rewards in terms of baseToken after adding the specified amount.
     */
    function getEntryShares(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 amount
    ) external view returns (uint256 returnedShares, uint256 expectedReward);

    /**
     * @notice Previews selling `shares` of an option side into the order book (mirrors sellOption).
     * @dev Walks the buy book from the best bid downward; `proceeds` is net of the maker rebate
     *      (exactly what the seller receives). `sharesSold` may be less than `shares` if the book
     *      is too thin to absorb the full size.
     * @param option The option being sold.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @param shares The number of shares the user wants to sell.
     * @return proceeds The base-token amount the seller receives.
     * @return sharesSold The number of shares actually filled against the buy book.
     */
    function getSellProceeds(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 shares
    ) external view returns (uint256 proceeds, uint256 sharesSold);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the shares and amounts allocated to each side when adding liquidity to an option.
     * @param option The option to add liquidity to.
     * @param totalAmount The total amount of base tokens being added as liquidity.
     * @return returnedShares An array containing the number of shares allocated to each side.
     * @return returnedAmounts An array containing the amount of base tokens allocated to each side.
     */
    function getReturnedLiquidity(
        uint256 option,
        uint256 totalAmount
    ) external view returns (uint256[] memory returnedShares, uint256[] memory returnedAmounts);

    /**
     * @notice Previews the YES/NO shares returned from the AMM when burning `lpShares`.
     * @dev Mirrors `removeLiquidity`'s proportional-reserve math. Frontends apply a
     *      slippage tolerance to the results to derive the `minYesOut` / `minNoOut`
     *      arguments. The returned amounts exclude the auto-merge step and accrued swap
     *      fees — they are purely the reserve withdrawal that the slippage guard checks.
     * @param option The option to remove liquidity from.
     * @param lpShares The number of LP shares to burn.
     * @return yesBack Expected YES shares withdrawn from the AMM reserve.
     * @return noBack Expected NO shares withdrawn from the AMM reserve.
     */
    function getRemovedLiquidity(
        uint256 option,
        uint256 lpShares
    ) external view returns (uint256 yesBack, uint256 noBack);

    /**
     * @notice Computes the price impact when a new amount is added to an option side.
     * @param option The index of the option being evaluated.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @param amount The amount being added to the option side.
     * @return The impacted price of the option side after adding the specified amount.
     */
    function getImpactedPrice(uint256 option, uint8 optionSide, uint256 amount) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the number of shares a user will receive when entering an option side.
     * @param option The option in which the user wants to enter.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @param amount The amount of base tokens the user is contributing.
     * @return The number of shares the user will receive.
     */
    function getReturnedShares(uint256 option, uint8 optionSide, uint256 amount) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the amount of base token required to move the AMM price
     *         of an option side to the desired target (CPMM model).
     * @param targetPrice The desired target price to reach.
     * @param option The option whose AMM reserves are used.
     * @param optionSide The side being bought (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @return requiredAmount The minimum base token amount required to reach `targetPrice`.
     */
    function getAmountRequired(
        uint256 targetPrice,
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide
    ) external view returns (uint256 requiredAmount);

    /**
     * @notice Retrieves the current price of an option side.
     * @param option The index of the option for which the price is being queried.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @return The current price of the specified option side.
     */
    function getCurrentPrice(uint256 option, uint8 optionSide) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the total cost of the next challenge on `option`, in the base token.
     * @dev The caller must approve exactly this figure. Which challenge is being priced follows
     * the option's state: an undisputed option is priced as a dispute, an already-disputed one as
     * an appeal. An appeal's non-refundable oracle charge (padded for swap slippage) is folded
     * into the returned amount; a dispute deploys no oracle, so it carries the stake alone.
     * @param option The option to price the next challenge for.
     * @return stake The full amount the challenger must approve, denominated in the base token.
     * The refundable collateral portion is returned in full if the challenger turns out to be
     * right and forfeited to the reward pot if they are wrong; any oracle charge included here is
     * never refunded.
     */
    function getDisputeAppealFee(uint256 option) external returns (uint256 stake);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the resolver bond required for resolution of a specific option.
     * @param option The option to calculate the bond for.
     * @return resolverBondAmount The resolver bond amount.
     */
    function getResolverBondAmount(uint256 option) external returns (uint256 resolverBondAmount);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the reward earned by a user from holding shares on the winning side of an option.
     * @param user The address of the user to calculate the shares reward for.
     * @param option The option to calculate the winning rewards for.
     * @return sharesReward The amount of reward tokens claimable by the user from winning shares.
     */
    function getSharesReward(address user, uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 sharesReward);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the reward earned by a user for providing liquidity to a specific option.
     * @param user The address of the user to calculate the liquidity reward for.
     * @param option The option to calculate the liquidity reward for.
     * @return liquidityReward The amount of reward tokens claimable by the user for liquidity provision.
     */
    function getLiquidityReward(address user, uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 liquidityReward);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the reward allocated to the pool creator for a specific option.
     * @param option The option to calculate the creator reward for.
     * @return creatorReward The amount of reward tokens claimable by the pool creator.
     */
    function getCreatorReward(uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 creatorReward);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the reward allocated to the resolver for a specific option.
     * @param option The option to calculate the resolver reward for.
     * @return resolverReward The amount of reward tokens claimable by the resolver.
     */
    function getResolverReward(uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 resolverReward);

    /**
     * @notice Total base-token amount a user will net when they claim an option.
     * @dev Mirrors `ClaimFacet.claim` + `_firstClaimCheck` (undisputed path): the winner pro-rata
     *      payout + LP swap fees, plus any role rewards the user is owed (creator if owner/referrer,
     *      closing if proposer, resolver share, resolver-bond refund). The oracle fixed fee is only
     *      included when the base token is USDT (it is otherwise paid separately in USDT). Returns 0
     *      once the user has already claimed or while the option is unresolved.
     * @param user The address that would call `claim`.
     * @param option The option being claimed.
     * @return totalClaimable The total base-token amount the user will receive.
     */
    function getClaimableAmount(address user, uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 totalClaimable);

    /**
     * @notice Whether `user` holds an economic position in `option`.
     * @dev True when the user holds outcome shares on either side, an AMM LP position, or base
     *      token escrowed in a resting buy order. Sell-order escrow needs no separate check —
     *      it is a subset of the gross share balance.
     *
     * @param option The option to test participation in.
     * @param user The address to test.
     * @return participant True when the user has a position in the option.
     */
    function isOptionParticipant(uint256 option, address user) external view returns (bool participant);
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

pragma solidity 0.8.26;

/**
 * @title IResolution
 * @author Rain Team
 * @notice Interface for the resolution facet.
 * @dev Defines the external functions for closing individual options and choosing
 * a winner per option within the Diamond architecture.
 */
interface IResolution {
    /* ===================================== FUNCTIONS ===================================== */

    /**
     * @notice Closes a specific option when the resolver is AI.
     * @dev The caller
     *      becomes the resolution proposer and may need to escrow a resolver bond.
     *      Marks the option as finalized and caches its end time.
     *
     *      Who may call, and when:
     *      - The pool owner (market creator): at any time.
     *      Participation is scoped per option: a stake in option 1 confers no right to
     *      close option 2. and can close after endtime + 30 minutes
     * @param option The option ID to close.
     */
    function closePool(uint256 option) external;

    /**
     * @notice Closes a specific option and proposes a winning side (non-AI resolver).
     * @dev Callable once the sale has opened, subject to the same caller gate as
     *      The caller becomes the resolution proposer and may need to escrow a resolver bond.
     *      Marks the option as finalized and records the proposed winner.
     * @param option The option ID to close.
     * @param proposedWinner The side proposed as winner (1 or 2).
     */
    function closePool(uint256 option, uint8 proposedWinner) external;

    /**
     * @notice Allows the AI resolver to choose the winning side for a specific option.
     * @dev Only callable by the resolver after the option has been finalized (closed).
     * @param option The option ID to resolve.
     * @param optionSide The winning side (1 or 2).
     */
    function chooseWinner(uint256 option, uint8 optionSide) external;

    /**
     * @notice Rejects a premature or invalid `closePool` proposal for a specific option.
     * @dev Callable only by the resolver after option finalization. The resolver bond
     *      escrowed by the proposer is FORFEITED and transferred to the resolver
     *      (`msg.sender`) as a slashing penalty for the incorrect close — it is NOT
     *      refunded to the original proposer. Resets resolution state so the option
     *      reopens for a new resolution attempt. Pre-existing order book orders are
     *      preserved in storage and remain cancellable.
     * @param option The option ID to revert resolution for.
     */
    function tooEarly(uint256 option) external;

    /**
     * @notice Reopens an appealed option whose oracle returned the "too early" verdict
     *         (winner == 3), meaning the option was resolved prematurely and every prior
     *         answer was wrong.
     * @dev Permissionless — fully driven by the on-chain oracle result. Requires the option
     *      to be in the `Appealed` state, finalized, unclaimed, and its appeal oracle to
     *      resolve to winner == 3. The resolver bond, first dispute fee, and appeal fee are
     *      all forfeited to the platform address, then the option is fully un-finalized so
     *      a fresh resolution cycle can run.
     * @param option The option ID to reopen.
     */
    function resolveAppealTooEarly(uint256 option) external;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity 0.8.26;

interface ITrading {
    /* ========================== FUNCTIONS ========================== */

    /**
     * @notice Allows a user to enter a voting option by depositing tokens.
     * @dev Transfers the specified `amount` of `baseToken` from the user to the contract and updates vote tallies.
     *      Reverts with `DeadlineExpired` if `block.timestamp > deadline` and with `SlippageExceeded` if the
     *      shares actually credited fall below `minSharesOut`. Pass `minSharesOut = 0` to disable the slippage
     *      check; pass a sufficiently large `deadline` (e.g. `type(uint256).max`) to disable the time check.
     * @param option The option ID the user is voting for.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 or 2).
     * @param amount The amount of `baseToken` being contributed.
     * @param minSharesOut Minimum acceptable total shares credited to the caller across the AMM swap and/or
     *                     OB walk. Reverts `SlippageExceeded` if not met.
     * @param deadline Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the call reverts `DeadlineExpired`.
     * @notice Emits an `EnterOption` event upon a successful contribution.
     */
    function enterOption(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 amount,
        uint256 minSharesOut,
        uint256 deadline
    ) external;

    /**
     * @notice Allows a user to provide liquidity to the pool.
     * @dev Transfers the specified amount of base tokens from the user to the contract.
     *      The YES/NO split deployed into the AMM is a function of the live reserve ratio
     *      at execution time. To protect against composition drift from concurrent
     *      deposits/swaps ordered ahead of this call, the caller declares the minimum
     *      amount of each side they are willing to have deployed. Reverts `DeadlineExpired`
     *      if `block.timestamp > deadline` and `SlippageExceeded` if either computed deposit
     *      side falls below its floor. Pass `minYesToDeposit = minNoToDeposit = 0` to disable
     *      the slippage check; pass a large `deadline` (e.g. `type(uint256).max`) to disable
     *      the time check.
     * @param option The option in which liquidity is added
     * @param totalAmount The total amount of base tokens the user is adding as liquidity.
     * @param minYesToDeposit Minimum YES shares the caller accepts seeding into the AMM.
     * @param minNoToDeposit Minimum NO shares the caller accepts seeding into the AMM.
     * @param deadline Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the call reverts `DeadlineExpired`.
     * @notice The function reverts if the pool sale is not live.
     * @notice Emits an `AddLiquidity` event for the liquidity addition.
     * @notice Emits an `EnterOption` event for each option's fund and vote update.
     * @notice Emits a `Price` event for each option to reflect the updated pool state.
     */
    function enterLiquidity(
        uint256 option,
        uint256 totalAmount,
        uint256 minYesToDeposit,
        uint256 minNoToDeposit,
        uint256 deadline
    ) external;

    /**
     * @notice Adds liquidity across every option in a single call.
     * @dev Distributes `totalAmount` base tokens across all options using per-option
     *      percentage weights in basis points. Each percentage must be at least 100 bps
     *      (1%), and the full array must sum to 10_000 (100%). Options that have been
     *      finalized mid-pool (e.g. an early resolver close) are skipped rather than
     *      reverting the whole batch; their slice is refunded to the caller after the
     *      loop, so liquidity still lands on the options that are still in Phase A.
     *      Reverts `PoolClosed` only once the pool-wide end time has passed (all options
     *      frozen). Per-option `minYesToDeposit` / `minNoToDeposit` floors guard each
     *      slice against reserve-ratio composition drift (same semantics as
     *      `enterLiquidity`); pass zeros to disable. Reverts `DeadlineExpired` if
     *      `block.timestamp > deadline`.
     * @param totalAmount Total base-token amount to deposit across every option.
     * @param percentages Per-option weights in basis points; length == numberOfOptions, sum == 10_000.
     * @param minYesToDeposit Per-option minimum YES shares seeded into the AMM; length == numberOfOptions.
     * @param minNoToDeposit Per-option minimum NO shares seeded into the AMM; length == numberOfOptions.
     * @param deadline Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the call reverts `DeadlineExpired`.
     * @notice Emits `EnterOption`, `AddLiquidity`, `ClaimSwapFees`, and `Price` per option (as applicable).
     */
    function enterLiquidityBatch(
        uint256 totalAmount,
        uint256[] calldata percentages,
        uint256[] calldata minYesToDeposit,
        uint256[] calldata minNoToDeposit,
        uint256 deadline
    ) external;

    /**
     * @notice Removes liquidity from a specific option's AMM.
     * @dev Burns `lpShares` LP tokens, withdraws proportional YES/NO reserves,
     *      merges matched pairs into base token collateral, and pays out any
     *      accrued swap fees. Only callable while the pool is not finalized.
     *      The YES/NO amounts returned track live reserves at execution time, so the
     *      caller declares the minimum of each side they will accept. Reverts
     *      `DeadlineExpired` if `block.timestamp > deadline` and `SlippageExceeded` if
     *      either returned side falls below its floor. Pass `minYesOut = minNoOut = 0` to
     *      disable the slippage check; pass a large `deadline` to disable the time check.
     * @param option The option to remove liquidity from.
     * @param lpShares The number of LP shares to burn.
     * @param minYesOut Minimum YES shares the caller accepts back from the AMM.
     * @param minNoOut Minimum NO shares the caller accepts back from the AMM.
     * @param deadline Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the call reverts `DeadlineExpired`.
     */
    function removeLiquidity(
        uint256 option,
        uint256 lpShares,
        uint256 minYesOut,
        uint256 minNoOut,
        uint256 deadline
    ) external;

    /**
     * @notice Market-sells `amount` shares of an option side into the resting buy book.
     * @dev Walks the buy book from the best bid down, filling as much of the `amount` as possible at each price level,
     * @param option The ID of the option to sell shares of.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 or 2).
     * @param amount The number of shares to sell.
     * @param minAmountOut Minimum acceptable NET base token received across all fills. Reverts
     *                     `SlippageExceeded` if not met. Pass `0` to disable the slippage check.
     * @param deadline Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the call reverts `DeadlineExpired`.
     */
    function sellOption(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 amount,
        uint256 minAmountOut,
        uint256 deadline
    ) external;

    /**
     * @notice Places a sell order for a specific option at a given price and amount.
     * @dev Allows a user to list their shares for sale in the order book.
     * @param option The ID of the option to sell shares for.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 or 2).
     * @param price The price per share at which to sell.
     * @param shares The total number of shares to sell.
     * @param postOnly Maker-only placement. When true, the matching loop is skipped and the
     *                 order rests directly; if `price` would cross a resting bid (i.e.
     *                 `price <= firstBuyOrderPrice`) the call reverts `OrderWouldCross`,
     *                 guaranteeing the caller is never charged taker fees (F-2026-17840).
     *                 When false, behaviour is unchanged: the order matches the buy book
     *                 first and rests only the residual.
     * @return orderID The unique identifier of the created order.
     */
    function placeSellOrder(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 price,
        uint256 shares,
        bool postOnly
    ) external returns (uint256 orderID);

    /**
     * @notice Places a buy order for a specific option at a given price and amount of base token.
     * @dev Allows a user to list a buy order in the order book.
     * @param option The ID of the option to buy shares for.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 or 2).
     * @param price The price per share at which to sell.
     * @param amount The total amount in terms of base token.
     * @param postOnly Maker-only placement. When true, the matching loop is skipped and the
     *                 order rests directly; if `price` would cross a resting ask (i.e.
     *                 `price >= firstSellOrderPrice`) the call reverts `OrderWouldCross`,
     *                 guaranteeing the caller is never charged taker fees (F-2026-17840).
     *                 When false, behaviour is unchanged: the order matches the sell book
     *                 first and rests only the residual.
     * @return orderID The unique identifier of the created order.
     */
    function placeBuyOrder(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 price,
        uint256 amount,
        bool postOnly
    ) external returns (uint256 orderID);

}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity 0.8.26;

/**
 * @title IInfo
 * @author Rain Team
 * @notice Interface for the rain pool info facet.
 * @dev Defines the external helper functions for the rain pool within the Diamond architecture.
 */
interface IInfo {
    /* ===================================== FUNCTIONS ===================================== */

    /**
     * @notice Returns the total number of active or created orders in the system.
     * @return The total number of orders.
     */
    function totalOrders() external returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the dynamic payout amount for a specific user on a specific option.
     * @param user The address of the user to calculate the dynamic payout for.
     * @param option The option to calculate the dynamic payout for.
     * @return dynamicPayout The amount of dynamic payout the user is eligible to receive for each side.
     */
    function getDynamicPayout(address user, uint256 option) external view returns (uint256[] memory dynamicPayout);

    /**
     * @notice Computes the amount of shares returned on the given amount for the specified option and side.
     * @param option The index of the option being evaluated.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @param amount The amount being added to the option.
     * @return returnedShares returned shares of the option side after adding the specified amount.
     * @return expectedReward returned expected rewards in terms of baseToken after adding the specified amount.
     */
    function getEntryShares(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 amount
    ) external view returns (uint256 returnedShares, uint256 expectedReward);

    /**
     * @notice Previews selling `shares` of an option side into the order book (mirrors sellOption).
     * @dev Walks the buy book from the best bid downward; `proceeds` is net of the maker rebate
     *      (exactly what the seller receives). `sharesSold` may be less than `shares` if the book
     *      is too thin to absorb the full size.
     * @param option The option being sold.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @param shares The number of shares the user wants to sell.
     * @return proceeds The base-token amount the seller receives.
     * @return sharesSold The number of shares actually filled against the buy book.
     */
    function getSellProceeds(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 shares
    ) external view returns (uint256 proceeds, uint256 sharesSold);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the shares and amounts allocated to each side when adding liquidity to an option.
     * @param option The option to add liquidity to.
     * @param totalAmount The total amount of base tokens being added as liquidity.
     * @return returnedShares An array containing the number of shares allocated to each side.
     * @return returnedAmounts An array containing the amount of base tokens allocated to each side.
     */
    function getReturnedLiquidity(
        uint256 option,
        uint256 totalAmount
    ) external view returns (uint256[] memory returnedShares, uint256[] memory returnedAmounts);

    /**
     * @notice Previews the YES/NO shares returned from the AMM when burning `lpShares`.
     * @dev Mirrors `removeLiquidity`'s proportional-reserve math. Frontends apply a
     *      slippage tolerance to the results to derive the `minYesOut` / `minNoOut`
     *      arguments. The returned amounts exclude the auto-merge step and accrued swap
     *      fees — they are purely the reserve withdrawal that the slippage guard checks.
     * @param option The option to remove liquidity from.
     * @param lpShares The number of LP shares to burn.
     * @return yesBack Expected YES shares withdrawn from the AMM reserve.
     * @return noBack Expected NO shares withdrawn from the AMM reserve.
     */
    function getRemovedLiquidity(
        uint256 option,
        uint256 lpShares
    ) external view returns (uint256 yesBack, uint256 noBack);

    /**
     * @notice Computes the price impact when a new amount is added to an option side.
     * @param option The index of the option being evaluated.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @param amount The amount being added to the option side.
     * @return The impacted price of the option side after adding the specified amount.
     */
    function getImpactedPrice(uint256 option, uint8 optionSide, uint256 amount) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the number of shares a user will receive when entering an option side.
     * @param option The option in which the user wants to enter.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @param amount The amount of base tokens the user is contributing.
     * @return The number of shares the user will receive.
     */
    function getReturnedShares(uint256 option, uint8 optionSide, uint256 amount) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the amount of base token required to move the AMM price
     *         of an option side to the desired target (CPMM model).
     * @param targetPrice The desired target price to reach.
     * @param option The option whose AMM reserves are used.
     * @param optionSide The side being bought (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @return requiredAmount The minimum base token amount required to reach `targetPrice`.
     */
    function getAmountRequired(
        uint256 targetPrice,
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide
    ) external view returns (uint256 requiredAmount);

    /**
     * @notice Retrieves the current price of an option side.
     * @param option The index of the option for which the price is being queried.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @return The current price of the specified option side.
     */
    function getCurrentPrice(uint256 option, uint8 optionSide) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the total cost of the next challenge on `option`, in the base token.
     * @dev The caller must approve exactly this figure. Which challenge is being priced follows
     * the option's state: an undisputed option is priced as a dispute, an already-disputed one as
     * an appeal. An appeal's non-refundable oracle charge (padded for swap slippage) is folded
     * into the returned amount; a dispute deploys no oracle, so it carries the stake alone.
     * @param option The option to price the next challenge for.
     * @return stake The full amount the challenger must approve, denominated in the base token.
     * The refundable collateral portion is returned in full if the challenger turns out to be
     * right and forfeited to the reward pot if they are wrong; any oracle charge included here is
     * never refunded.
     */
    function getDisputeAppealFee(uint256 option) external returns (uint256 stake);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the resolver bond required for resolution of a specific option.
     * @param option The option to calculate the bond for.
     * @return resolverBondAmount The resolver bond amount.
     */
    function getResolverBondAmount(uint256 option) external returns (uint256 resolverBondAmount);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the reward earned by a user from holding shares on the winning side of an option.
     * @param user The address of the user to calculate the shares reward for.
     * @param option The option to calculate the winning rewards for.
     * @return sharesReward The amount of reward tokens claimable by the user from winning shares.
     */
    function getSharesReward(address user, uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 sharesReward);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the reward earned by a user for providing liquidity to a specific option.
     * @param user The address of the user to calculate the liquidity reward for.
     * @param option The option to calculate the liquidity reward for.
     * @return liquidityReward The amount of reward tokens claimable by the user for liquidity provision.
     */
    function getLiquidityReward(address user, uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 liquidityReward);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the reward allocated to the pool creator for a specific option.
     * @param option The option to calculate the creator reward for.
     * @return creatorReward The amount of reward tokens claimable by the pool creator.
     */
    function getCreatorReward(uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 creatorReward);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the reward allocated to the resolver for a specific option.
     * @param option The option to calculate the resolver reward for.
     * @return resolverReward The amount of reward tokens claimable by the resolver.
     */
    function getResolverReward(uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 resolverReward);

    /**
     * @notice Total base-token amount a user will net when they claim an option.
     * @dev Mirrors `ClaimFacet.claim` + `_firstClaimCheck` (undisputed path): the winner pro-rata
     *      payout + LP swap fees, plus any role rewards the user is owed (creator if owner/referrer,
     *      closing if proposer, resolver share, resolver-bond refund). The oracle fixed fee is only
     *      included when the base token is USDT (it is otherwise paid separately in USDT). Returns 0
     *      once the user has already claimed or while the option is unresolved.
     * @param user The address that would call `claim`.
     * @param option The option being claimed.
     * @return totalClaimable The total base-token amount the user will receive.
     */
    function getClaimableAmount(address user, uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 totalClaimable);

    /**
     * @notice Whether `user` holds an economic position in `option`.
     * @dev True when the user holds outcome shares on either side, an AMM LP position, or base
     *      token escrowed in a resting buy order. Sell-order escrow needs no separate check —
     *      it is a subset of the gross share balance.
     *
     * @param option The option to test participation in.
     * @param user The address to test.
     * @return participant True when the user has a position in the option.
     */
    function isOptionParticipant(uint256 option, address user) external view returns (bool participant);
}
