// SPDX-License-Identifier:

pragma solidity 0.8.26;

/**
 * @title IClaim
 * @author Rain Team
 * @notice Interface for the claim facet.
 * @dev Defines the external functions for claiming rewards within the Diamond architecture.
 */
interface IClaim {
    /* ===================================== FUNCTIONS ===================================== */

    /**
     * @notice Allows users to claim their winnings or liquidity rewards after an option has resolved.
     * @dev This function verifies whether the winner has been determined for the given option.
     *      - In public pools, it ensures the oracle has finalized the winner.
     *      - The function checks if the caller has already claimed their rewards for this option.
     *      - Rewards are calculated based on LP shares and winning-side shares.
     * @param option The option ID to claim rewards for.
     * @notice Reverts if:
     *      - The option is invalid.
     *      - The winner has not been determined.
     *      - The option is still open.
     *      - The user has already claimed rewards for this option.
     *      - The user is not eligible to claim any rewards.
     * @notice Emits a `Claim` event upon successful reward distribution.
     */
    function claim(uint256 option) external;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity 0.8.26;

interface ITrading {
    /* ========================== FUNCTIONS ========================== */

    /**
     * @notice Allows a user to enter a voting option by depositing tokens.
     * @dev Transfers the specified `amount` of `baseToken` from the user to the contract and updates vote tallies.
     *      Reverts with `DeadlineExpired` if `block.timestamp > deadline` and with `SlippageExceeded` if the
     *      shares actually credited fall below `minSharesOut`. Pass `minSharesOut = 0` to disable the slippage
     *      check; pass a sufficiently large `deadline` (e.g. `type(uint256).max`) to disable the time check.
     * @param option The option ID the user is voting for.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 or 2).
     * @param amount The amount of `baseToken` being contributed.
     * @param minSharesOut Minimum acceptable total shares credited to the caller across the AMM swap and/or
     *                     OB walk. Reverts `SlippageExceeded` if not met.
     * @param deadline Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the call reverts `DeadlineExpired`.
     * @notice Emits an `EnterOption` event upon a successful contribution.
     */
    function enterOption(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 amount,
        uint256 minSharesOut,
        uint256 deadline
    ) external;

    /**
     * @notice Allows a user to provide liquidity to the pool.
     * @dev Transfers the specified amount of base tokens from the user to the contract.
     *      The YES/NO split deployed into the AMM is a function of the live reserve ratio
     *      at execution time. To protect against composition drift from concurrent
     *      deposits/swaps ordered ahead of this call, the caller declares the minimum
     *      amount of each side they are willing to have deployed. Reverts `DeadlineExpired`
     *      if `block.timestamp > deadline` and `SlippageExceeded` if either computed deposit
     *      side falls below its floor. Pass `minYesToDeposit = minNoToDeposit = 0` to disable
     *      the slippage check; pass a large `deadline` (e.g. `type(uint256).max`) to disable
     *      the time check.
     * @param option The option in which liquidity is added
     * @param totalAmount The total amount of base tokens the user is adding as liquidity.
     * @param minYesToDeposit Minimum YES shares the caller accepts seeding into the AMM.
     * @param minNoToDeposit Minimum NO shares the caller accepts seeding into the AMM.
     * @param deadline Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the call reverts `DeadlineExpired`.
     * @notice The function reverts if the pool sale is not live.
     * @notice Emits an `AddLiquidity` event for the liquidity addition.
     * @notice Emits an `EnterOption` event for each option's fund and vote update.
     * @notice Emits a `Price` event for each option to reflect the updated pool state.
     */
    function enterLiquidity(
        uint256 option,
        uint256 totalAmount,
        uint256 minYesToDeposit,
        uint256 minNoToDeposit,
        uint256 deadline
    ) external;

    /**
     * @notice Adds liquidity across every option in a single call.
     * @dev Distributes `totalAmount` base tokens across all options using per-option
     *      percentage weights in basis points. Each percentage must be at least 100 bps
     *      (1%), and the full array must sum to 10_000 (100%). Options that have been
     *      finalized mid-pool (e.g. an early resolver close) are skipped rather than
     *      reverting the whole batch; their slice is refunded to the caller after the
     *      loop, so liquidity still lands on the options that are still in Phase A.
     *      Reverts `PoolClosed` only once the pool-wide end time has passed (all options
     *      frozen). Per-option `minYesToDeposit` / `minNoToDeposit` floors guard each
     *      slice against reserve-ratio composition drift (same semantics as
     *      `enterLiquidity`); pass zeros to disable. Reverts `DeadlineExpired` if
     *      `block.timestamp > deadline`.
     * @param totalAmount Total base-token amount to deposit across every option.
     * @param percentages Per-option weights in basis points; length == numberOfOptions, sum == 10_000.
     * @param minYesToDeposit Per-option minimum YES shares seeded into the AMM; length == numberOfOptions.
     * @param minNoToDeposit Per-option minimum NO shares seeded into the AMM; length == numberOfOptions.
     * @param deadline Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the call reverts `DeadlineExpired`.
     * @notice Emits `EnterOption`, `AddLiquidity`, `ClaimSwapFees`, and `Price` per option (as applicable).
     */
    function enterLiquidityBatch(
        uint256 totalAmount,
        uint256[] calldata percentages,
        uint256[] calldata minYesToDeposit,
        uint256[] calldata minNoToDeposit,
        uint256 deadline
    ) external;

    /**
     * @notice Removes liquidity from a specific option's AMM.
     * @dev Burns `lpShares` LP tokens, withdraws proportional YES/NO reserves,
     *      merges matched pairs into base token collateral, and pays out any
     *      accrued swap fees. Only callable while the pool is not finalized.
     *      The YES/NO amounts returned track live reserves at execution time, so the
     *      caller declares the minimum of each side they will accept. Reverts
     *      `DeadlineExpired` if `block.timestamp > deadline` and `SlippageExceeded` if
     *      either returned side falls below its floor. Pass `minYesOut = minNoOut = 0` to
     *      disable the slippage check; pass a large `deadline` to disable the time check.
     * @param option The option to remove liquidity from.
     * @param lpShares The number of LP shares to burn.
     * @param minYesOut Minimum YES shares the caller accepts back from the AMM.
     * @param minNoOut Minimum NO shares the caller accepts back from the AMM.
     * @param deadline Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the call reverts `DeadlineExpired`.
     */
    function removeLiquidity(
        uint256 option,
        uint256 lpShares,
        uint256 minYesOut,
        uint256 minNoOut,
        uint256 deadline
    ) external;

    /**
     * @notice Market-sells `amount` shares of an option side into the resting buy book.
     * @dev Walks the buy book from the best bid down, filling as much of the `amount` as possible at each price level,
     * @param option The ID of the option to sell shares of.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 or 2).
     * @param amount The number of shares to sell.
     * @param minAmountOut Minimum acceptable NET base token received across all fills. Reverts
     *                     `SlippageExceeded` if not met. Pass `0` to disable the slippage check.
     * @param deadline Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the call reverts `DeadlineExpired`.
     */
    function sellOption(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 amount,
        uint256 minAmountOut,
        uint256 deadline
    ) external;

    /**
     * @notice Places a sell order for a specific option at a given price and amount.
     * @dev Allows a user to list their shares for sale in the order book.
     * @param option The ID of the option to sell shares for.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 or 2).
     * @param price The price per share at which to sell.
     * @param shares The total number of shares to sell.
     * @param postOnly Maker-only placement. When true, the matching loop is skipped and the
     *                 order rests directly; if `price` would cross a resting bid (i.e.
     *                 `price <= firstBuyOrderPrice`) the call reverts `OrderWouldCross`,
     *                 guaranteeing the caller is never charged taker fees (F-2026-17840).
     *                 When false, behaviour is unchanged: the order matches the buy book
     *                 first and rests only the residual.
     * @return orderID The unique identifier of the created order.
     */
    function placeSellOrder(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 price,
        uint256 shares,
        bool postOnly
    ) external returns (uint256 orderID);

    /**
     * @notice Places a buy order for a specific option at a given price and amount of base token.
     * @dev Allows a user to list a buy order in the order book.
     * @param option The ID of the option to buy shares for.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 or 2).
     * @param price The price per share at which to sell.
     * @param amount The total amount in terms of base token.
     * @param postOnly Maker-only placement. When true, the matching loop is skipped and the
     *                 order rests directly; if `price` would cross a resting ask (i.e.
     *                 `price >= firstSellOrderPrice`) the call reverts `OrderWouldCross`,
     *                 guaranteeing the caller is never charged taker fees (F-2026-17840).
     *                 When false, behaviour is unchanged: the order matches the sell book
     *                 first and rests only the residual.
     * @return orderID The unique identifier of the created order.
     */
    function placeBuyOrder(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 price,
        uint256 amount,
        bool postOnly
    ) external returns (uint256 orderID);

}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

pragma solidity 0.8.26;

/**
 * @title IResolution
 * @author Rain Team
 * @notice Interface for the resolution facet.
 * @dev Defines the external functions for closing individual options and choosing
 * a winner per option within the Diamond architecture.
 */
interface IResolution {
    /* ===================================== FUNCTIONS ===================================== */

    /**
     * @notice Closes a specific option when the resolver is AI.
     * @dev The caller
     *      becomes the resolution proposer and may need to escrow a resolver bond.
     *      Marks the option as finalized and caches its end time.
     *
     *      Who may call, and when:
     *      - The pool owner (market creator): at any time.
     *      Participation is scoped per option: a stake in option 1 confers no right to
     *      close option 2. and can close after endtime + 30 minutes
     * @param option The option ID to close.
     */
    function closePool(uint256 option) external;

    /**
     * @notice Closes a specific option and proposes a winning side (non-AI resolver).
     * @dev Callable once the sale has opened, subject to the same caller gate as
     *      The caller becomes the resolution proposer and may need to escrow a resolver bond.
     *      Marks the option as finalized and records the proposed winner.
     * @param option The option ID to close.
     * @param proposedWinner The side proposed as winner (1 or 2).
     */
    function closePool(uint256 option, uint8 proposedWinner) external;

    /**
     * @notice Allows the AI resolver to choose the winning side for a specific option.
     * @dev Only callable by the resolver after the option has been finalized (closed).
     * @param option The option ID to resolve.
     * @param optionSide The winning side (1 or 2).
     */
    function chooseWinner(uint256 option, uint8 optionSide) external;

    /**
     * @notice Rejects a premature or invalid `closePool` proposal for a specific option.
     * @dev Callable only by the resolver after option finalization. The resolver bond
     *      escrowed by the proposer is FORFEITED and transferred to the resolver
     *      (`msg.sender`) as a slashing penalty for the incorrect close — it is NOT
     *      refunded to the original proposer. Resets resolution state so the option
     *      reopens for a new resolution attempt. Pre-existing order book orders are
     *      preserved in storage and remain cancellable.
     * @param option The option ID to revert resolution for.
     */
    function tooEarly(uint256 option) external;

    /**
     * @notice Reopens an appealed option whose oracle returned the "too early" verdict
     *         (winner == 3), meaning the option was resolved prematurely and every prior
     *         answer was wrong.
     * @dev Permissionless — fully driven by the on-chain oracle result. Requires the option
     *      to be in the `Appealed` state, finalized, unclaimed, and its appeal oracle to
     *      resolve to winner == 3. The resolver bond, first dispute fee, and appeal fee are
     *      all forfeited to the platform address, then the option is fully un-finalized so
     *      a fresh resolution cycle can run.
     * @param option The option ID to reopen.
     */
    function resolveAppealTooEarly(uint256 option) external;
}

CutNotQueued().notice: No proposal with this id is currently queued.

CutAlreadyQueued().notice: This exact cut payload is already queued. Cancel it or execute it first.

UpgradesDisabled().notice: This pool was created with `upgradeDelay == 0` and is immutable.

CutProposalExpired().notice: The proposal sat past its grace period and can no longer be executed.

InvalidUpgradeDelay().notice: The delay baked into this pool at creation is outside the hard-coded bounds.

CutTimelockNotElapsed().notice: The delay has not elapsed yet.

DiamondCutExecuted(bytes32).notice: A queued facet cut has been executed. Always paired with a {DiamondCut}.

DiamondCutCancelled(bytes32).notice: A queued facet cut has been withdrawn before execution.

DiamondCutQueued(bytes32,uint256,(addres.notice: A facet cut has been queued and becomes executable at `eta`.

userdoc.notice: Upgrade surface for a pool diamond. Every write is gated to `ds.FACTORY` — the         RainDeployer, whose owner is the protocol multisig — and every post-construction cut         must sit queued for `upgradeDelay` before it can be applied.         There is deliberately NO instant-cut path, not even a pause. If an emergency         entrypoint is ever wanted it must be proposed as its own change with its own scope,         not folded in here.         Pools created with `upgradeDelay == 0` are immutable and revert on every path below.         The heavy lifting is implemented in LibDiamond.

upgradeDelay().notice: Seconds between queueing and executability. Fixed at pool creation; `0` means the         pool is immutable and every cut path reverts.

cutEta(bytes32).notice: Earliest execution timestamp for `proposalId`, or `0` if not queued.

upgradeGracePeriod().notice: Window after `eta` during which a queued cut stays executable.

cancelDiamondCut(bytes32).notice: Withdraw a queued cut before it executes.

diamondCut((address,uint8,bytes4[])[],ad.notice: Add/replace/remove any number of functions and optionally execute         a function with delegatecall

executeDiamondCut((address,uint8,bytes4[.notice: Apply a previously queued cut. The payload must hash to a queued proposal whose         `eta` has passed and whose grace period has not.

proposeDiamondCut((address,uint8,bytes4[.notice: Queue a facet cut. Executable once `upgradeDelay` has elapsed.

diamondCutProposalId((address,uint8,byte.notice: Proposal id for a cut payload. Pure helper — mirrors the id the pool derives.

DiamondCutQueued(bytes32,uint256,(addres.details: Emitted before any state the cut describes is applied. The full cut payload is      carried in the event so the queued upgrade is publicly reviewable during the delay      without needing the proposer to publish it off-chain.

params._init: The address of the contract or facet to execute _calldata
params._calldata: A function call, including function selector and arguments                  _calldata is executed with delegatecall on _init
params._diamondCut: Contains the facet addresses and function selectors

diamondCut((address,uint8,bytes4[])[],ad.details: Construction-time only. `LibDiamond.diamondCut` latches `isInitialized`, so on a      live pool this reverts `AlreadyInitialized` — the instant path stays closed.

proposeDiamondCut((address,uint8,bytes4[.details: Caller must be the deployer (`ds.FACTORY`), whose owner is the protocol multisig.

returns.proposalId: Hash identifying this exact cut payload.

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity 0.8.26;

interface ITrading {
    /* ========================== FUNCTIONS ========================== */

    /**
     * @notice Allows a user to enter a voting option by depositing tokens.
     * @dev Transfers the specified `amount` of `baseToken` from the user to the contract and updates vote tallies.
     *      Reverts with `DeadlineExpired` if `block.timestamp > deadline` and with `SlippageExceeded` if the
     *      shares actually credited fall below `minSharesOut`. Pass `minSharesOut = 0` to disable the slippage
     *      check; pass a sufficiently large `deadline` (e.g. `type(uint256).max`) to disable the time check.
     * @param option The option ID the user is voting for.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 or 2).
     * @param amount The amount of `baseToken` being contributed.
     * @param minSharesOut Minimum acceptable total shares credited to the caller across the AMM swap and/or
     *                     OB walk. Reverts `SlippageExceeded` if not met.
     * @param deadline Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the call reverts `DeadlineExpired`.
     * @notice Emits an `EnterOption` event upon a successful contribution.
     */
    function enterOption(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 amount,
        uint256 minSharesOut,
        uint256 deadline
    ) external;

    /**
     * @notice Allows a user to provide liquidity to the pool.
     * @dev Transfers the specified amount of base tokens from the user to the contract.
     *      The YES/NO split deployed into the AMM is a function of the live reserve ratio
     *      at execution time. To protect against composition drift from concurrent
     *      deposits/swaps ordered ahead of this call, the caller declares the minimum
     *      amount of each side they are willing to have deployed. Reverts `DeadlineExpired`
     *      if `block.timestamp > deadline` and `SlippageExceeded` if either computed deposit
     *      side falls below its floor. Pass `minYesToDeposit = minNoToDeposit = 0` to disable
     *      the slippage check; pass a large `deadline` (e.g. `type(uint256).max`) to disable
     *      the time check.
     * @param option The option in which liquidity is added
     * @param totalAmount The total amount of base tokens the user is adding as liquidity.
     * @param minYesToDeposit Minimum YES shares the caller accepts seeding into the AMM.
     * @param minNoToDeposit Minimum NO shares the caller accepts seeding into the AMM.
     * @param deadline Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the call reverts `DeadlineExpired`.
     * @notice The function reverts if the pool sale is not live.
     * @notice Emits an `AddLiquidity` event for the liquidity addition.
     * @notice Emits an `EnterOption` event for each option's fund and vote update.
     * @notice Emits a `Price` event for each option to reflect the updated pool state.
     */
    function enterLiquidity(
        uint256 option,
        uint256 totalAmount,
        uint256 minYesToDeposit,
        uint256 minNoToDeposit,
        uint256 deadline
    ) external;

    /**
     * @notice Adds liquidity across every option in a single call.
     * @dev Distributes `totalAmount` base tokens across all options using per-option
     *      percentage weights in basis points. Each percentage must be at least 100 bps
     *      (1%), and the full array must sum to 10_000 (100%). Options that have been
     *      finalized mid-pool (e.g. an early resolver close) are skipped rather than
     *      reverting the whole batch; their slice is refunded to the caller after the
     *      loop, so liquidity still lands on the options that are still in Phase A.
     *      Reverts `PoolClosed` only once the pool-wide end time has passed (all options
     *      frozen). Per-option `minYesToDeposit` / `minNoToDeposit` floors guard each
     *      slice against reserve-ratio composition drift (same semantics as
     *      `enterLiquidity`); pass zeros to disable. Reverts `DeadlineExpired` if
     *      `block.timestamp > deadline`.
     * @param totalAmount Total base-token amount to deposit across every option.
     * @param percentages Per-option weights in basis points; length == numberOfOptions, sum == 10_000.
     * @param minYesToDeposit Per-option minimum YES shares seeded into the AMM; length == numberOfOptions.
     * @param minNoToDeposit Per-option minimum NO shares seeded into the AMM; length == numberOfOptions.
     * @param deadline Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the call reverts `DeadlineExpired`.
     * @notice Emits `EnterOption`, `AddLiquidity`, `ClaimSwapFees`, and `Price` per option (as applicable).
     */
    function enterLiquidityBatch(
        uint256 totalAmount,
        uint256[] calldata percentages,
        uint256[] calldata minYesToDeposit,
        uint256[] calldata minNoToDeposit,
        uint256 deadline
    ) external;

    /**
     * @notice Removes liquidity from a specific option's AMM.
     * @dev Burns `lpShares` LP tokens, withdraws proportional YES/NO reserves,
     *      merges matched pairs into base token collateral, and pays out any
     *      accrued swap fees. Only callable while the pool is not finalized.
     *      The YES/NO amounts returned track live reserves at execution time, so the
     *      caller declares the minimum of each side they will accept. Reverts
     *      `DeadlineExpired` if `block.timestamp > deadline` and `SlippageExceeded` if
     *      either returned side falls below its floor. Pass `minYesOut = minNoOut = 0` to
     *      disable the slippage check; pass a large `deadline` to disable the time check.
     * @param option The option to remove liquidity from.
     * @param lpShares The number of LP shares to burn.
     * @param minYesOut Minimum YES shares the caller accepts back from the AMM.
     * @param minNoOut Minimum NO shares the caller accepts back from the AMM.
     * @param deadline Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the call reverts `DeadlineExpired`.
     */
    function removeLiquidity(
        uint256 option,
        uint256 lpShares,
        uint256 minYesOut,
        uint256 minNoOut,
        uint256 deadline
    ) external;

    /**
     * @notice Market-sells `amount` shares of an option side into the resting buy book.
     * @dev Walks the buy book from the best bid down, filling as much of the `amount` as possible at each price level,
     * @param option The ID of the option to sell shares of.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 or 2).
     * @param amount The number of shares to sell.
     * @param minAmountOut Minimum acceptable NET base token received across all fills. Reverts
     *                     `SlippageExceeded` if not met. Pass `0` to disable the slippage check.
     * @param deadline Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the call reverts `DeadlineExpired`.
     */
    function sellOption(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 amount,
        uint256 minAmountOut,
        uint256 deadline
    ) external;

    /**
     * @notice Places a sell order for a specific option at a given price and amount.
     * @dev Allows a user to list their shares for sale in the order book.
     * @param option The ID of the option to sell shares for.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 or 2).
     * @param price The price per share at which to sell.
     * @param shares The total number of shares to sell.
     * @param postOnly Maker-only placement. When true, the matching loop is skipped and the
     *                 order rests directly; if `price` would cross a resting bid (i.e.
     *                 `price <= firstBuyOrderPrice`) the call reverts `OrderWouldCross`,
     *                 guaranteeing the caller is never charged taker fees (F-2026-17840).
     *                 When false, behaviour is unchanged: the order matches the buy book
     *                 first and rests only the residual.
     * @return orderID The unique identifier of the created order.
     */
    function placeSellOrder(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 price,
        uint256 shares,
        bool postOnly
    ) external returns (uint256 orderID);

    /**
     * @notice Places a buy order for a specific option at a given price and amount of base token.
     * @dev Allows a user to list a buy order in the order book.
     * @param option The ID of the option to buy shares for.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 or 2).
     * @param price The price per share at which to sell.
     * @param amount The total amount in terms of base token.
     * @param postOnly Maker-only placement. When true, the matching loop is skipped and the
     *                 order rests directly; if `price` would cross a resting ask (i.e.
     *                 `price >= firstSellOrderPrice`) the call reverts `OrderWouldCross`,
     *                 guaranteeing the caller is never charged taker fees (F-2026-17840).
     *                 When false, behaviour is unchanged: the order matches the sell book
     *                 first and rests only the residual.
     * @return orderID The unique identifier of the created order.
     */
    function placeBuyOrder(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 price,
        uint256 amount,
        bool postOnly
    ) external returns (uint256 orderID);

}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity 0.8.26;

/**
 * @title IInfo
 * @author Rain Team
 * @notice Interface for the rain pool info facet.
 * @dev Defines the external helper functions for the rain pool within the Diamond architecture.
 */
interface IInfo {
    /* ===================================== FUNCTIONS ===================================== */

    /**
     * @notice Returns the total number of active or created orders in the system.
     * @return The total number of orders.
     */
    function totalOrders() external returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the dynamic payout amount for a specific user on a specific option.
     * @param user The address of the user to calculate the dynamic payout for.
     * @param option The option to calculate the dynamic payout for.
     * @return dynamicPayout The amount of dynamic payout the user is eligible to receive for each side.
     */
    function getDynamicPayout(address user, uint256 option) external view returns (uint256[] memory dynamicPayout);

    /**
     * @notice Computes the amount of shares returned on the given amount for the specified option and side.
     * @param option The index of the option being evaluated.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @param amount The amount being added to the option.
     * @return returnedShares returned shares of the option side after adding the specified amount.
     * @return expectedReward returned expected rewards in terms of baseToken after adding the specified amount.
     */
    function getEntryShares(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 amount
    ) external view returns (uint256 returnedShares, uint256 expectedReward);

    /**
     * @notice Previews selling `shares` of an option side into the order book (mirrors sellOption).
     * @dev Walks the buy book from the best bid downward; `proceeds` is net of the maker rebate
     *      (exactly what the seller receives). `sharesSold` may be less than `shares` if the book
     *      is too thin to absorb the full size.
     * @param option The option being sold.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @param shares The number of shares the user wants to sell.
     * @return proceeds The base-token amount the seller receives.
     * @return sharesSold The number of shares actually filled against the buy book.
     */
    function getSellProceeds(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 shares
    ) external view returns (uint256 proceeds, uint256 sharesSold);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the shares and amounts allocated to each side when adding liquidity to an option.
     * @param option The option to add liquidity to.
     * @param totalAmount The total amount of base tokens being added as liquidity.
     * @return returnedShares An array containing the number of shares allocated to each side.
     * @return returnedAmounts An array containing the amount of base tokens allocated to each side.
     */
    function getReturnedLiquidity(
        uint256 option,
        uint256 totalAmount
    ) external view returns (uint256[] memory returnedShares, uint256[] memory returnedAmounts);

    /**
     * @notice Previews the YES/NO shares returned from the AMM when burning `lpShares`.
     * @dev Mirrors `removeLiquidity`'s proportional-reserve math. Frontends apply a
     *      slippage tolerance to the results to derive the `minYesOut` / `minNoOut`
     *      arguments. The returned amounts exclude the auto-merge step and accrued swap
     *      fees — they are purely the reserve withdrawal that the slippage guard checks.
     * @param option The option to remove liquidity from.
     * @param lpShares The number of LP shares to burn.
     * @return yesBack Expected YES shares withdrawn from the AMM reserve.
     * @return noBack Expected NO shares withdrawn from the AMM reserve.
     */
    function getRemovedLiquidity(
        uint256 option,
        uint256 lpShares
    ) external view returns (uint256 yesBack, uint256 noBack);

    /**
     * @notice Computes the price impact when a new amount is added to an option side.
     * @param option The index of the option being evaluated.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @param amount The amount being added to the option side.
     * @return The impacted price of the option side after adding the specified amount.
     */
    function getImpactedPrice(uint256 option, uint8 optionSide, uint256 amount) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the number of shares a user will receive when entering an option side.
     * @param option The option in which the user wants to enter.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @param amount The amount of base tokens the user is contributing.
     * @return The number of shares the user will receive.
     */
    function getReturnedShares(uint256 option, uint8 optionSide, uint256 amount) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the amount of base token required to move the AMM price
     *         of an option side to the desired target (CPMM model).
     * @param targetPrice The desired target price to reach.
     * @param option The option whose AMM reserves are used.
     * @param optionSide The side being bought (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @return requiredAmount The minimum base token amount required to reach `targetPrice`.
     */
    function getAmountRequired(
        uint256 targetPrice,
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide
    ) external view returns (uint256 requiredAmount);

    /**
     * @notice Retrieves the current price of an option side.
     * @param option The index of the option for which the price is being queried.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @return The current price of the specified option side.
     */
    function getCurrentPrice(uint256 option, uint8 optionSide) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates what the next challenge on `option` costs, split into its two components.
     * @dev The caller must approve `stake + oracleCost`; approving `stake` alone reverts.
     * Which challenge is being priced follows the option's state: an undisputed option is priced
     * as a dispute, an already-disputed one as an appeal.
     * @param option The option to price the next challenge for.
     * @return stake The refundable collateral, denominated in the base token. Returned in full if
     * the challenger turns out to be right, forfeited to the reward pot if they are wrong.
     * @return oracleCost The non-refundable charge that funds the oracle this challenge deploys,
     * denominated in the base token and padded for swap slippage. Always 0 for a dispute, which
     * deploys no oracle.
     */
    function getDisputeAppealFee(uint256 option) external returns (uint256 stake, uint256 oracleCost);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the resolver bond required for resolution of a specific option.
     * @param option The option to calculate the bond for.
     * @return resolverBondAmount The resolver bond amount.
     */
    function getResolverBondAmount(uint256 option) external returns (uint256 resolverBondAmount);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the reward earned by a user from holding shares on the winning side of an option.
     * @param user The address of the user to calculate the shares reward for.
     * @param option The option to calculate the winning rewards for.
     * @return sharesReward The amount of reward tokens claimable by the user from winning shares.
     */
    function getSharesReward(address user, uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 sharesReward);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the reward earned by a user for providing liquidity to a specific option.
     * @param user The address of the user to calculate the liquidity reward for.
     * @param option The option to calculate the liquidity reward for.
     * @return liquidityReward The amount of reward tokens claimable by the user for liquidity provision.
     */
    function getLiquidityReward(address user, uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 liquidityReward);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the reward allocated to the pool creator for a specific option.
     * @param option The option to calculate the creator reward for.
     * @return creatorReward The amount of reward tokens claimable by the pool creator.
     */
    function getCreatorReward(uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 creatorReward);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the reward allocated to the resolver for a specific option.
     * @param option The option to calculate the resolver reward for.
     * @return resolverReward The amount of reward tokens claimable by the resolver.
     */
    function getResolverReward(uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 resolverReward);

    /**
     * @notice Total base-token amount a user will net when they claim an option.
     * @dev Mirrors `ClaimFacet.claim` + `_firstClaimCheck` (undisputed path): the winner pro-rata
     *      payout + LP swap fees, plus any role rewards the user is owed (creator if owner/referrer,
     *      closing if proposer, resolver share, resolver-bond refund). The oracle fixed fee is only
     *      included when the base token is USDT (it is otherwise paid separately in USDT). Returns 0
     *      once the user has already claimed or while the option is unresolved.
     * @param user The address that would call `claim`.
     * @param option The option being claimed.
     * @return totalClaimable The total base-token amount the user will receive.
     */
    function getClaimableAmount(address user, uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 totalClaimable);

    /**
     * @notice Whether `user` holds an economic position in `option`.
     * @dev True when the user holds outcome shares on either side, an AMM LP position, or base
     *      token escrowed in a resting buy order. Sell-order escrow needs no separate check —
     *      it is a subset of the gross share balance.
     *
     * @param option The option to test participation in.
     * @param user The address to test.
     * @return participant True when the user has a position in the option.
     */
    function isOptionParticipant(uint256 option, address user) external view returns (bool participant);
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

pragma solidity 0.8.26;

/**
 * @title IResolution
 * @author Rain Team
 * @notice Interface for the resolution facet.
 * @dev Defines the external functions for closing individual options and choosing
 * a winner per option within the Diamond architecture.
 */
interface IResolution {
    /* ===================================== FUNCTIONS ===================================== */

    /**
     * @notice Closes a specific option when the resolver is AI.
     * @dev The caller
     *      becomes the resolution proposer and may need to escrow a resolver bond.
     *      Marks the option as finalized and caches its end time.
     *
     *      Who may call, and when:
     *      - The pool owner (market creator): at any time.
     *      Participation is scoped per option: a stake in option 1 confers no right to
     *      close option 2. and can close after endtime + 30 minutes
     * @param option The option ID to close.
     */
    function closePool(uint256 option) external;

    /**
     * @notice Closes a specific option and proposes a winning side (non-AI resolver).
     * @dev Callable once the sale has opened, subject to the same caller gate as
     *      The caller becomes the resolution proposer and may need to escrow a resolver bond.
     *      Marks the option as finalized and records the proposed winner.
     * @param option The option ID to close.
     * @param proposedWinner The side proposed as winner (1 or 2).
     */
    function closePool(uint256 option, uint8 proposedWinner) external;

    /**
     * @notice Allows the AI resolver to choose the winning side for a specific option.
     * @dev Only callable by the resolver after the option has been finalized (closed).
     * @param option The option ID to resolve.
     * @param optionSide The winning side (1 or 2).
     */
    function chooseWinner(uint256 option, uint8 optionSide) external;

    /**
     * @notice Rejects a premature or invalid `closePool` proposal for a specific option.
     * @dev Callable only by the resolver after option finalization. The resolver bond
     *      escrowed by the proposer is FORFEITED and transferred to the resolver
     *      (`msg.sender`) as a slashing penalty for the incorrect close — it is NOT
     *      refunded to the original proposer. Resets resolution state so the option
     *      reopens for a new resolution attempt. Pre-existing order book orders are
     *      preserved in storage and remain cancellable.
     * @param option The option ID to revert resolution for.
     */
    function tooEarly(uint256 option) external;

    /**
     * @notice Reopens an appealed option whose oracle returned the "too early" verdict
     *         (winner == 3), meaning the option was resolved prematurely and every prior
     *         answer was wrong.
     * @dev Permissionless — fully driven by the on-chain oracle result. Requires the option
     *      to be in the `Appealed` state, finalized, unclaimed, and its appeal oracle to
     *      resolve to winner == 3. The resolver bond, first dispute fee, and appeal fee are
     *      all forfeited to the platform address, then the option is fully un-finalized so
     *      a fresh resolution cycle can run.
     * @param option The option ID to reopen.
     */
    function resolveAppealTooEarly(uint256 option) external;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity 0.8.26;

/**
 * @title IRainAccounting
 * @notice Interface for the RainAccounting contract.
 */
interface IRainAccounting {
    /* ========================== EVENTS ======================================== */

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a pool reports tokens flowing in.
     * @param pool The reporting pool.
     * @param token The token whose balance moved.
     * @param amount The inflow, in the token's own decimals.
     * @param totalHeld The protocol-wide total for `token` after the inflow.
     */
    event RecordedIncrease(address indexed pool, address indexed token, uint256 amount, uint256 totalHeld);

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a pool reports tokens flowing out.
     * @dev `amount` is the outflow ACTUALLY applied to the ledger, which is smaller than the
     *      reported one whenever {UnderflowClamped} fires alongside it. Summing this field
     *      reproduces `totalHeld` exactly; summing the reported figure does not.
     * @param pool The reporting pool.
     * @param token The token whose balance moved.
     * @param amount The outflow applied, in the token's own decimals.
     * @param totalHeld The protocol-wide total for `token` after the outflow.
     */
    event RecordedDecrease(address indexed pool, address indexed token, uint256 amount, uint256 totalHeld);

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when an outflow would have driven the ledger below zero.
     * @dev Signals that an inflow was never recorded -- a pool funded before the ledger was
     *      wired up, a token sent directly to a pool address, or an entrypoint missing its hook.
     *      Should never fire in steady state; treat it as a page, not a warning.
     *
     *      Clamped to zero rather than reverting: the gap is a bookkeeping one, and blocking a
     *      withdrawal over it would be the wrong trade. The event is how it surfaces instead.
     * @param pool The reporting pool.
     * @param token The token whose balance moved.
     * @param requested The outflow the pool reported.
     * @param available The ledger balance that was actually on the books.
     */
    event UnderflowClamped(address indexed pool, address indexed token, uint256 requested, uint256 available);

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a new token is seen for the first time and added to the tracked set.
     * @param token The newly tracked token.
     */
    event TokenTracked(address indexed token);

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when the pool registry used for authorization changes.
     * @param previousDeployer The previous registry.
     * @param newDeployer The new registry.
     */
    event DeployerSet(address indexed previousDeployer, address indexed newDeployer);

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a pool's manual authorization override changes.
     * @param pool The pool whose override changed.
     * @param authorized The new override value.
     */
    event PoolOverrideSet(address indexed pool, bool authorized);

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when the USDR solvency gate configuration changes.
     * @param solvencyEngine The Solvency Engine read for the predicate, or zero when unset.
     * @param enabled Whether inflows are gated on it.
     */
    event SolvencyGateSet(address indexed solvencyEngine, bool enabled);

    /* ========================== ERRORS ======================================== */

    /// @notice Thrown when a zero or otherwise unusable address is supplied.
    error InvalidAddress();

    /// @notice Thrown when the caller is neither a registered pool nor a manually authorized one.
    error NotAuthorizedPool();

    /**
     * @notice Thrown when money would enter the protocol while USDR's solvency rule is broken.
     * @dev Only inflows trip this. Outflows are never gated -- a user must always be able to get
     *      their money out, whatever state USDR is in.
     */
    error SolvencyGateActive();

    /* ========================== FUNCTIONS ===================================== */

    /**
     * @notice Records tokens flowing into the caller.
     * @dev Callable only by a pool registered on {deployer}, or one manually authorized via
     *      {setPoolOverride}. Pools report the NET change measured across a whole entrypoint
     *      (balance after minus balance before), not per individual transfer -- measuring the
     *      real balance is what keeps the ledger from drifting when a transfer path is missed
     *      or a token takes a fee on transfer.
     *
     *      REVERTS with {SolvencyGateActive} when the gate is on and USDR's solvency rule is
     *      broken. The pool-side call is un-wrapped precisely so this can stop a trade.
     *
     *      Naming deliberately mirrors USDR's `ReserveAccounting`, which this is the
     *      prediction-market counterpart of.
     * @param token The token whose balance moved.
     * @param amount The inflow, in the token's own decimals. Zero is a no-op.
     */
    function recordIncrease(address token, uint256 amount) external;

    /**
     * @notice Records tokens flowing out of the caller against the protocol-wide ledger.
     * @dev Same authorization and measurement contract as {recordIncrease}.
     *
     *      An outflow larger than the ledger holds is clamped to zero and raises
     *      {UnderflowClamped} rather than reverting -- see that event for why.
     * @param token The token whose balance moved.
     * @param amount The outflow, in the token's own decimals. Zero is a no-op.
     */
    function recordDecrease(address token, uint256 amount) external;

    /**
     * @notice The protocol-wide amount of `token` held across every reporting pool.
     * @dev Denominated in the token's own decimals, NOT normalized to wad. Consumers that need a
     *      USD figure must scale it themselves.
     * @param token The token to query.
     * @return The total held.
     */
    function totalHeld(address token) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Compares the ledger against the live on-chain balances of a set of pools.
     * @dev Drift detection for monitoring. The pool list is supplied by the caller so the loop
     *      stays bounded -- deliberately not a self-enumerating aggregate, because the pool set is
     *      unbounded and would eventually exceed any node's eth_call gas cap.
     *
     *      `actualSum` only equals `ledgerTotal` when `pools` is the COMPLETE set of pools that
     *      have reported for `token`. For a partial batch, compare per-batch across runs rather
     *      than reading `drift` as an absolute.
     * @param token The token to reconcile.
     * @param pools The pools to sum live balances over.
     * @return ledgerTotal The value currently on the books.
     * @return actualSum The summed live balance of the supplied pools.
     * @return drift `actualSum - ledgerTotal`.
     */
    function reconcile(
        address token,
        address[] calldata pools
    ) external view returns (uint256 ledgerTotal, uint256 actualSum, int256 drift);

    /**
     * @notice Whether USDR's solvency rule is currently broken.
     * @dev USDR's own formula, evaluated live:
     *
     *          worstCaseLoss() > breachThreshold()
     *
     *      Both sides come from the engine, so the reserve arithmetic stays on USDR's side of the
     *      boundary. Their stored `breached` flag is deliberately NOT used -- it only reflects the
     *      last `checkInvariant()` and goes stale during a keeper outage.
     *
     *      FAILS OPEN. If the engine reverts this returns false. Failing closed would let a bug in
     *      a contract we do not control halt every Rain pool, and USDR defends its own invariant
     *      anyway. This gate is a second layer, not the first.
     * @return True when the rule is broken and inflows should be blocked.
     */
    function solvencyBreached() external view returns (bool);

    /**
     * @notice The live inputs to the predicate, for monitoring.
     * @return worstCaseLoss USDR's stressed worst-case loss [wad].
     * @return threshold USDR's breach threshold [wad].
     * @return ok False when the reads failed; the other two are then meaningless.
     */
    function solvencyState() external view returns (uint256 worstCaseLoss, uint256 threshold, bool ok);

    /**
     * @notice Points the gate at USDR and switches it on or off.
     * @dev Ships disabled so the ledger can be observed first. Enabling it makes every inflow
     *      entrypoint in every pool depend on two external reads, one of which loops over USDR's
     *      volatile collateral -- price that before turning it on.
     * @param newSolvencyEngine The USDR Solvency Engine.
     * @param enabled Whether to gate inflows.
     */
    function setSolvencyGate(address newSolvencyEngine, bool enabled) external;

    /**
     * @notice Whether an address may call {recordIncrease} and {recordDecrease}.
     * @param pool The address to check.
     * @return True when the address is a registered or manually authorized pool.
     */
    function isAuthorizedPool(address pool) external view returns (bool);

    /**
     * @notice Every token that has ever been recorded.
     * @return The tracked token set.
     */
    function trackedTokens() external view returns (address[] memory);

    /**
     * @notice The number of tokens that have ever been recorded.
     * @return The size of the tracked token set.
     */
    function trackedTokensLength() external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice The pool registry consulted for authorization.
     * @return The RainDeployer address.
     */
    function deployer() external view returns (address);

    /**
     * @notice Manual authorization override for a pool.
     * @param pool The pool to query.
     * @return True when the pool is authorized irrespective of the registry.
     */
    function poolOverride(address pool) external view returns (bool);

    /**
     * @notice Points the ledger at a different pool registry.
     * @param newDeployer The new RainDeployer address.
     */
    function setDeployer(address newDeployer) external;

    /**
     * @notice Manually authorizes or de-authorizes a pool.
     * @dev Escape hatch for pools that are not (or no longer) in the registry -- a migration to
     *      a new deployer above all. Not needed in the normal path.
     * @param pool The pool to change.
     * @param authorized The new override value.
     */
    function setPoolOverride(address pool, bool authorized) external;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity 0.8.26;

/**
 * @title IInfo
 * @author Rain Team
 * @notice Interface for the rain pool info facet.
 * @dev Defines the external helper functions for the rain pool within the Diamond architecture.
 */
interface IInfo {
    /* ===================================== FUNCTIONS ===================================== */

    /**
     * @notice Returns the total number of active or created orders in the system.
     * @return The total number of orders.
     */
    function totalOrders() external returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the dynamic payout amount for a specific user on a specific option.
     * @param user The address of the user to calculate the dynamic payout for.
     * @param option The option to calculate the dynamic payout for.
     * @return dynamicPayout The amount of dynamic payout the user is eligible to receive for each side.
     */
    function getDynamicPayout(address user, uint256 option) external view returns (uint256[] memory dynamicPayout);

    /**
     * @notice Computes the amount of shares returned on the given amount for the specified option and side.
     * @param option The index of the option being evaluated.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @param amount The amount being added to the option.
     * @return returnedShares returned shares of the option side after adding the specified amount.
     * @return expectedReward returned expected rewards in terms of baseToken after adding the specified amount.
     */
    function getEntryShares(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 amount
    ) external view returns (uint256 returnedShares, uint256 expectedReward);

    /**
     * @notice Previews selling `shares` of an option side into the order book (mirrors sellOption).
     * @dev Walks the buy book from the best bid downward; `proceeds` is net of the maker rebate
     *      (exactly what the seller receives). `sharesSold` may be less than `shares` if the book
     *      is too thin to absorb the full size.
     * @param option The option being sold.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @param shares The number of shares the user wants to sell.
     * @return proceeds The base-token amount the seller receives.
     * @return sharesSold The number of shares actually filled against the buy book.
     */
    function getSellProceeds(
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide,
        uint256 shares
    ) external view returns (uint256 proceeds, uint256 sharesSold);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the shares and amounts allocated to each side when adding liquidity to an option.
     * @param option The option to add liquidity to.
     * @param totalAmount The total amount of base tokens being added as liquidity.
     * @return returnedShares An array containing the number of shares allocated to each side.
     * @return returnedAmounts An array containing the amount of base tokens allocated to each side.
     */
    function getReturnedLiquidity(
        uint256 option,
        uint256 totalAmount
    ) external view returns (uint256[] memory returnedShares, uint256[] memory returnedAmounts);

    /**
     * @notice Previews the YES/NO shares returned from the AMM when burning `lpShares`.
     * @dev Mirrors `removeLiquidity`'s proportional-reserve math. Frontends apply a
     *      slippage tolerance to the results to derive the `minYesOut` / `minNoOut`
     *      arguments. The returned amounts exclude the auto-merge step and accrued swap
     *      fees — they are purely the reserve withdrawal that the slippage guard checks.
     * @param option The option to remove liquidity from.
     * @param lpShares The number of LP shares to burn.
     * @return yesBack Expected YES shares withdrawn from the AMM reserve.
     * @return noBack Expected NO shares withdrawn from the AMM reserve.
     */
    function getRemovedLiquidity(
        uint256 option,
        uint256 lpShares
    ) external view returns (uint256 yesBack, uint256 noBack);

    /**
     * @notice Computes the price impact when a new amount is added to an option side.
     * @param option The index of the option being evaluated.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @param amount The amount being added to the option side.
     * @return The impacted price of the option side after adding the specified amount.
     */
    function getImpactedPrice(uint256 option, uint8 optionSide, uint256 amount) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the number of shares a user will receive when entering an option side.
     * @param option The option in which the user wants to enter.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @param amount The amount of base tokens the user is contributing.
     * @return The number of shares the user will receive.
     */
    function getReturnedShares(uint256 option, uint8 optionSide, uint256 amount) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates the amount of base token required to move the AMM price
     *         of an option side to the desired target (CPMM model).
     * @param targetPrice The desired target price to reach.
     * @param option The option whose AMM reserves are used.
     * @param optionSide The side being bought (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @return requiredAmount The minimum base token amount required to reach `targetPrice`.
     */
    function getAmountRequired(
        uint256 targetPrice,
        uint256 option,
        uint8 optionSide
    ) external view returns (uint256 requiredAmount);

    /**
     * @notice Retrieves the current price of an option side.
     * @param option The index of the option for which the price is being queried.
     * @param optionSide The side of the option (1 = Yes, 2 = No).
     * @return The current price of the specified option side.
     */
    function getCurrentPrice(uint256 option, uint8 optionSide) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @notice Calculates what the next challenge on `option` costs, split into its two components.
     * @dev The caller must approve `stake + oracleCost`; approving `stake` alone reverts.
     * Which challenge is being priced follows the option's state: an undisputed option is priced
     * as a dispute, an already-disputed one as an appeal.
     * @param option The option to price the next challenge for.
     * @return stake The refundable collateral, denominated in the base token. Returned in full if
     * the challenger turns out to be right, forfeited to the reward pot if they are wrong.
     * @return oracleCost The non-refundable charge that funds the oracle this challenge deploys,
     * denominated in the base token and padded for swap slippage. Always 0 for a dispute, which
     * deploys no oracle.
     */
    function getDisputeAppealFee(uint256 option) external returns (uint256 stake, uint256 oracleCost);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the resolver bond required for resolution of a specific option.
     * @param option The option to calculate the bond for.
     * @return resolverBondAmount The resolver bond amount.
     */
    function getResolverBondAmount(uint256 option) external returns (uint256 resolverBondAmount);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the reward earned by a user from holding shares on the winning side of an option.
     * @param user The address of the user to calculate the shares reward for.
     * @param option The option to calculate the winning rewards for.
     * @return sharesReward The amount of reward tokens claimable by the user from winning shares.
     */
    function getSharesReward(address user, uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 sharesReward);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the reward earned by a user for providing liquidity to a specific option.
     * @param user The address of the user to calculate the liquidity reward for.
     * @param option The option to calculate the liquidity reward for.
     * @return liquidityReward The amount of reward tokens claimable by the user for liquidity provision.
     */
    function getLiquidityReward(address user, uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 liquidityReward);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the reward allocated to the pool creator for a specific option.
     * @param option The option to calculate the creator reward for.
     * @return creatorReward The amount of reward tokens claimable by the pool creator.
     */
    function getCreatorReward(uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 creatorReward);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the reward allocated to the resolver for a specific option.
     * @param option The option to calculate the resolver reward for.
     * @return resolverReward The amount of reward tokens claimable by the resolver.
     */
    function getResolverReward(uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 resolverReward);

    /**
     * @notice Total base-token amount a user will net when they claim an option.
     * @dev Mirrors `ClaimFacet.claim` + `_firstClaimCheck` (undisputed path): the winner pro-rata
     *      payout + LP swap fees, plus any role rewards the user is owed (creator if owner/referrer,
     *      closing if proposer, resolver share, resolver-bond refund). The oracle fixed fee is only
     *      included when the base token is USDT (it is otherwise paid separately in USDT). Returns 0
     *      once the user has already claimed or while the option is unresolved.
     * @param user The address that would call `claim`.
     * @param option The option being claimed.
     * @return totalClaimable The total base-token amount the user will receive.
     */
    function getClaimableAmount(address user, uint256 option) external view returns (uint256 totalClaimable);

    /**
     * @notice Whether `user` holds an economic position in `option`.
     * @dev True when the user holds outcome shares on either side, an AMM LP position, or base
     *      token escrowed in a resting buy order. Sell-order escrow needs no separate check —
     *      it is a subset of the gross share balance.
     *
     * @param option The option to test participation in.
     * @param user The address to test.
     * @return participant True when the user has a position in the option.
     */
    function isOptionParticipant(uint256 option, address user) external view returns (bool participant);
}

pragma solidity 0.8.26;

/**
 * @title IClaim
 * @author Rain Team
 * @notice Interface for the claim facet.
 * @dev Defines the external functions for claiming rewards within the Diamond architecture.
 */
interface IClaim {
    /* ===================================== FUNCTIONS ===================================== */

    /**
     * @notice Allows users to claim their winnings or liquidity rewards after an option has resolved.
     * @dev This function verifies whether the winner has been determined for the given option.
     *      - In public pools, it ensures the oracle has finalized the winner.
     *      - The function checks if the caller has already claimed their rewards for this option.
     *      - Rewards are calculated based on LP shares and winning-side shares.
     * @param option The option ID to claim rewards for.
     * @notice Reverts if:
     *      - The option is invalid.
     *      - The winner has not been determined.
     *      - The option is still open.
     *      - The user has already claimed rewards for this option.
     *      - The user is not eligible to claim any rewards.
     * @notice Emits a `Claim` event upon successful reward distribution.
     */
    function claim(uint256 option) external;
}
